books.name: बालकाण्डम्
books.es: King Daśaratha performs a sacrifice to obtain sons. Four brothers are born to his queens. The sage Viśvāmitra takes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to protect his forest sacrifice from demons. Rāma kills the demoness Tāṭakā and subdues Mārīca. In Mithilā, Rāma strings and breaks the bow of Śiva, winning Sītā in marriage. The four brothers marry the daughters and nieces of King Janaka. On the return journey, Rāma subdues the warrior-sage Paraśurāma.
books.subtitle: The birth of Rāma and subsequent marriage to Sītā.

books.name: अयोध्याकाण्डम्
books.es: Daśaratha prepares to crown Rāma as prince regent. Queen Kaikeyī, prompted by her maid Mantharā, invokes two old boons: the coronation of her son Bharata and Rāma's fourteen-year exile. Rāma departs for the forest with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa. Daśaratha dies of grief. Bharata refuses the throne and visits Rāma at Citrakūṭa to request his return. Rāma insists on fulfilling the vow. Bharata takes Rāma's sandals to rule as a deputy from Nandigrāma.
books.subtitle: Rāma is exiled and Bharata refuses the throne.

books.name: अरण्यकाण्डम्
books.es: The trio enters the Daṇḍaka forest. Lakṣmaṇa mutilates the demoness Śūrpaṇakhā after she attacks Sītā. Her brothers Khara and Dūṣaṇa lead an army against Rāma but are killed. In revenge, Rāvaṇa uses Mārīca as a golden deer to lure the brothers away. Rāvaṇa abducts Sītā and mortally wounds the vulture Jaṭāyu. Searching for Sītā, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa meet the demon Kabandha and the ascetic Śabarī, who direct them toward the vānara tribes.
books.subtitle: Sītā is abducted by Rāvaṇa in the forest.

books.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डम्
books.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa reach Ṛṣyamūka mountain and ally with the vānara Sugrīva. Rāma kills Sugrīva's brother Vālin to restore Sugrīva to the throne. Sugrīva mobilizes a vānara army to locate Sītā. Four search parties head in cardinal directions. The southern group, led by Aṅgada and Hanumān, learns from the vulture Sampāti that Sītā is held in Laṅkā. Hanumān reaches the ocean shore and prepares to leap across.
books.subtitle: Rāma allies with Sugrīva to find Sītā.

books.name: सुन्दरकाण्डम्
books.es: Hanumān leaps to Laṅkā and discovers Sītā in the Aśoka grove. He presents Rāma's signet ring as proof of his identity. Sītā gives him her jewel as a token for the King. Hanumān destroys the grove and is captured by Indrajit. When Rāvaṇa sets Hanumān's tail on fire, Hanumān escapes and burns the city of Laṅkā. He returns across the ocean and informs Rāma of Sītā's location and welfare.
books.subtitle: Hanumān finds Sītā in Laṅkā.

books.name: युद्धकाण्डम्
books.es: Rāma's army builds a bridge to Laṅkā. Vibhīṣaṇa defects from Rāvaṇa to join Rāma. A war ensues where Kumbhakarṇa and Indrajit are killed. Rāma kills Rāvaṇa with a Brahmāstra. Sītā undergoes an ordeal by fire to verify her conduct. After the term of exile ends, Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa return to Ayodhyā on the Puṣpaka vimāna. Rāma is crowned king, establishing a reign of order.
books.subtitle: Rāma defeats Rāvaṇa and is crowned king.

books.name: उत्तरकाण्डम्
books.es: Rāma hears public rumors regarding Sītā and banishes her. Sītā takes refuge at the hermitage of Vālmīki, where she bears twins, Lava and Kuśa. The twins sing the Rāmāyaṇa at Rāma's sacrifice. Rāma recognizes his sons and Sītā returns to the earth. Rāma eventually divides the kingdom among his heirs. He and his brothers enter the Sarayū river to return to their original cosmic forms, concluding the lineage's earthly reign.
books.subtitle: Rāma's final years and Sītā's departure.

chapters.subtitle: A summary of the life and reign of Rāma.
chapters.es: A prince of the Ikṣvāku line named Rāma possesses a conch-shaped neck and arms reaching his knees. To fulfill a paternal vow, he enters the Daṇḍaka forest with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa. When Rāvaṇa abducts Sītā, Rāma forms an alliance with vānaras, bridges the ocean, and kills the rākṣasa king. Returning to his capital, he leads a reign where no mother outlives her child and the people live free from disease for eleven thousand years.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे प्रथमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Vālmīki creates the first śloka.
chapters.es: Vālmīki walks to the Tamasā river with his disciple Bharadvāja and observes a pair of krauñca birds. When a niṣāda hunter kills the male, Vālmīki utters a spontaneous curse. This rhythmic expression, born from his śoka, becomes the first śloka. Brahmā arrives to reveal that this poetic form emerged by his will. He commands Vālmīki to use the meter to narrate the history of Rāma, promising that the story will endure as long as mountains remain.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Vālmīki perceives the life of Rāma through meditation.
chapters.es: After performing ācamana and sitting on darbha grass, Vālmīki meditates to perceive the life of Rāma. He sees the breaking of the bow, the forest exile, and the death of Daśaratha. The vision follows the alliance with Hanumān, the construction of the ocean bridge, and the defeat of Rāvaṇa. Rāma returns to Ayodhyā for his coronation, but the record also includes future events, such as the banishment of Sītā, contained within the final Uttarakāṇḍa.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे तृतीयः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Kuśa and Lava chant the epic for Rāma.
chapters.es: After composing the history of Rāma, the sage initiates Kuśa and Lava into the poem. Dressed as ascetics, the twins master the seven jāti melodies and the nine rasas. They chant the verses before an assembly of forest dwellers, receiving water pots and bark garments as rewards. Later, they recite the work on the city roads. Rāma invites them to his palace, where they sing the epic before the throne while the king and his brothers listen.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: A description of the city of Ayodhyā.
chapters.es: The kings of the Ikṣvāku line, descending from Manu, govern Kosala along the Sarayū river. Daśaratha resides in Ayodhyā, a city spanning twelve yojanas with wide highways sprinkled with water and strewn with flowers. Fortified by deep moats and śataghnī missiles, the capital houses tiered palaces, mango groves, and markets. Vīṇā and mṛdaṅga music sounds through streets filled with horses, elephants, and Vedic scholars. Merchants and tributary kings gather here, supporting a city stocked with grain.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे पञ्चमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha rules Ayodhyā according to dharma.
chapters.es: Daśaratha governs Ayodhyā with the righteousness of Manu. Every resident possesses wealth, cattle, and grain, appearing as pure as maharṣis. Men and women wear golden kuṇḍala earrings and fragrant garlands, living in a city free from hunger or atheism. High-bred horses from Kāmboja and mountain-sized elephants fill the stables. Warriors trained in weaponry guard the fortified gates while the four varṇa groups perform their traditional rituals. No citizen remains unlearned in this secure capital.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha governs with his ministers and priests.
chapters.es: Daśaratha governs his realm alongside eight ministers, including Sumantra and Siddhārtha, and the royal priests Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva. These counselors employ a network of spies to monitor internal and foreign affairs while maintaining the treasury and army. They enforce the law impartially, imposing daṇḍa even upon their own sons. Under their guidance, the city of Ayodhyā remains free of falsehood. The king presides over the earth like the rising sun surrounded by its rays.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha hears a prophecy regarding Ṛśyaśṛṅga.
chapters.es: Daśaratha resolves to perform a vājimedha sacrifice to obtain an heir. He summons his ministers and priests to prepare the ritual. His counselor Sumantra recounts a prophecy by Sanatkumāra concerning the ascetic Ṛśyaśṛṅga. This youth, raised in isolation by Vibhāṇḍaka, once ended a drought in Aṅga after being lured there by courtesans and marrying Śāntā. Sumantra identifies this sage as the one destined to grant Daśaratha sons.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे अष्टमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Courtesans lure Ṛṣyaśṛṅga to Aṅga.
chapters.es: Sumantra recounts how Romapāda’s ministers lured Ṛṣyaśṛṅga to their kingdom. Unfamiliar with women, the young ascetic meets a group of courtesans who offer him sweetmeats. Mistaking these for forest fruits, he becomes restless after they depart. When they return, he follows them to the city. His arrival triggers immediate rainfall across the parched land. Romapāda welcomes the sage and grants him his daughter, Śāntā, in marriage to ensure his continued presence.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे नवमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha brings Ṛṣyaśṛṅga to Ayodhyā.
chapters.es: Daśaratha travels to Aṅga to seek Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, following a prophecy by Sanatkumāra. He asks Romapāda to allow the sage and Śāntā to return with him to Ayodhyā to conduct a yajña for sons. Romapāda agrees, and Daśaratha escorts them back to his kingdom. Citizens decorate the city and sound conches and drums as the party enters. The king welcomes Ṛṣyaśṛṅga into the inner apartments, where the royal ladies greet Śāntā.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे दशमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha prepares an aśvamedha for heirs.
chapters.es: Daśaratha, seeking heirs, resolves to perform a horse sacrifice as spring begins. He bows before Ṛṣyaśṛṅga and summons his priests, including Vasiṣṭha and Jābāli. The king orders the release of the ritual horse and the construction of a sacrificial ground on the northern bank of the Sarayū. The brāhmaṇas approve the plan, promising four sons. To prevent interference from brahmarākṣasas, Daśaratha commands his ministers to ensure every rite follows scriptural law.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकादशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha invites guests to the sacrifice.
chapters.es: As spring returns, the king enters the sacrificial pavilion to begin rites for sons. Vasiṣṭha commands architects to build brick structures and residences. Sumantra travels to invite the kings of Mithilā, Kāśī, and Kekaya, who arrive bearing gifts. Vasiṣṭha instructs that all guests receive food and honor without contempt. Once Daśaratha enters the yajñāyatana on an auspicious day, he joins Vasiṣṭha and Ṛśyaśṛṅga to initiate the ceremony according to scriptural tradition.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे द्वादशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha performs the horse sacrifice.
chapters.es: Daśaratha commences the aśvamedha on the northern bank of the Sarayū. Priests led by Ṛśyaśṛṅga erect golden yūpa posts and build an altar in the shape of a golden-winged garuḍa. While guests eat, Kausalyā strikes the sacrificial horse with a scimitar. The priests offer the horse's limbs into the flames, and the king inhales the smoke to cleanse his sins. After distributing gold and cows, Ṛśyaśṛṅga promises the king four sons to continue his dynasty.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे त्रयोदशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The deities petition Viṣṇu for help.
chapters.es: Ṛśyaśṛṅga begins the putrīyeṣṭi sacrifice to secure sons for Daśaratha. As deities gather, they petition Brahmā to stop the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa. Brahmā explains that Rāvaṇa is immune to gods but vulnerable to humans. When Viṣṇu appears, the gods ask him to divide his essence and take birth as the four sons of Daśaratha’s wives. This plan facilitates the destruction of the demon king.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे चतुर्दशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha receives divine pāyasa for his queens.
chapters.es: Viṣṇu agrees to take human form to slay Rāvaṇa, who is protected by a boon against all beings except mortals. As Daśaratha performs a sacrifice, a dark figure emerges from the flames holding a golden vessel of divine pāyasa. This messenger commands the king to distribute the food among his queens. Daśaratha divides the offering among Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and Kaikeyī. The wives consume the gift, ensuring the birth of sons.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे पञ्चदशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The gods father vānaras to assist Rāma.
chapters.es: Brahmā commands celestial beings to father sons who will assist Viṣṇu. The gods, sages, and spirits produce offspring in the forms of monkeys and bears. These vānaras possess the strength of mountains and change their shapes at will. They fight using trees and boulders, leap across oceans, and seize clouds. Led by Vālī and Sugrīva, thousands of these warriors inhabit the forests and peaks, readying themselves to support Rāma against Rāvaṇa.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे षोडशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The birth of the princes and Viśvāmitra's arrival.
chapters.es: Daśaratha returns to Ayodhyā. Kausalyā gives birth to Rāma, while Kaikeyī and Sumitrā bear Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa, and Śatrughna as portions of Viṣṇu. The brothers master the Veda and weapons. Lakṣmaṇa remains inseparable from Rāma. As the king ponders his sons' marriages, the sage Viśvāmitra reaches the palace. Daśaratha greets the guest with arghya, offering to perform any task the sage requires to ensure his satisfaction.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे सप्तदशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra requests Rāma to protect his sacrifice.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra requests that Daśaratha send Rāma to protect his sacrifice from the rākṣasas Mārīca and Subāhu, who defile the altar with blood. The sage explains that his ritual prevents him from uttering curses, making the young prince's protection necessary. He describes the youth as kākapakṣadhara and promises him fame. Despite the sage's assurances of Rāma’s power, Daśaratha trembles and sinks into his throne, overcome by the prospect of parting with his son.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे अष्टादशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha refuses to part with Rāma.
chapters.es: Daśaratha collapses in fear upon hearing the request for his son. He argues that Rāma is under sixteen years old and unskilled in the warfare of rākṣasas. Offering himself and an akṣauhiṇī army instead, the king cites his sixty thousand years of childless longing as reason to keep the boy safe. Even as the sage identifies the threats of Mārīca and Subāhu, the king refuses to part with his eldest son, fearing the prowess of Rāvaṇa.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकोनविंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Vasiṣṭha advises Daśaratha to fulfill his promise.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra reacts with wrath to the king’s hesitation, causing the earth to shake. Vasiṣṭha intervenes, reminding Daśaratha that breaking a promise destroys accumulated iṣṭāpūrta. He describes the sage’s command over the hundred astra born from the daughters of Dakṣa. These weapons change forms to overcome any rākṣasa. Vasiṣṭha insists that Rāma remains safe under the protection of this sage who holds the ancient knowledge of Kṛśāśva’s sons.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे विंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa learn the balā mantras.
chapters.es: Daśaratha entrusts Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to Viśvāmitra. As the brothers follow the sage, celestial drums sound and flowers fall. Rāma, wearing kākapakṣa side-locks, carries his bow. After walking half a yojana to the Sarayū’s southern bank, Viśvāmitra initiates Rāma into the balā and atibalā mantras. This knowledge shields him from hunger, thirst, and fatigue. Rāma touches water to purify himself, accepts the chants, and rests on the riverbank.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकविंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The princes visit the site of Kāma's destruction.
chapters.es: At daybreak, Viśvāmitra wakes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. After performing morning rites, the princes travel to the confluence of the Sarayū and Gaṅgā. Viśvāmitra explains that the nearby hermitage is where Śiva’s third eye once consumed the god of love, Kāma. This act left the deity anaṅga, or bodiless, giving the region of Aṅga its name. The resident ascetics welcome the travelers to stay the night.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे द्वाविंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Rāma crosses the Gaṅgā to Tāṭakā's forest.
chapters.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa cross the Gaṅgā by boat. A tumultuous roar marks where the Sarayū meets the Gaṅgā. Reaching the southern bank, they enter a forest of dhava and bilva trees. Viśvāmitra explains that these grounds, once the realms of Malada and Karūṣa, were blessed by Indra. The sage identifies the source of the wasteland’s decay as the yakṣiṇī Tāṭakā and orders Rāma to strike her down with his own strength.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra explains the origins of Tāṭakā.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra explains that the yakṣa Suketu received his daughter Taṭakā as a gift from Brahmā. After her husband dies, Taṭakā and her son Mārīca attack Agastya, who curses them into man-eating rākṣasas. Viśvāmitra commands Rāma to kill her to protect cows and brāhmaṇas. He cites Indra slaying Mantharā and Viṣṇu killing Bhṛgu’s wife as historical precedents for a prince’s duty to eliminate those who abandon dharma.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे चतुर्विंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Rāma slays the yakṣiṇī Tāṭakā.
chapters.es: Rāma vows to follow the instructions of Viśvāmitra, honoring the command of Daśaratha. To protect cows and brāhmaṇas, he twangs his bow, drawing Tāṭakā from the forest. Though initially reluctant to kill a woman, Rāma responds to her charging attack by piercing her chest with an arrow. After the yakṣiṇī falls, Indra and the gods urge Viśvāmitra to bestow divine weapons upon the prince. The group then rests at the riverbank.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे पञ्चविंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra bestows celestial astra upon Rāma.
chapters.es: After daybreak, Viśvāmitra grants Rāma an array of celestial astra. He bestows the dharmacakra, kālacakra, the trident of Śiva, and the brahmāstra. Rāma receives the modakī and śikharī maces, along with various pāśa and thunderbolts. Facing east, the sage recites mantra sequences to transfer the weapons. The presiding deities of these arms appear to offer their service. Rāma touches the weapons and bids them reside in his mind before resuming his journey.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे षड्विंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Rāma learns the saṃhāra mantras.
chapters.es: Rāma undergoes purification to receive the saṃhāra mantras, allowing him to withdraw the divine weapons. These weapons appear in personified forms to pledge their service. Rāma commands them to depart and return only when summoned. Resuming their walk, the travelers leave the forest for a region of lush trees. Rāma notices a mountain grove teeming with deer and asks Viśvāmitra to explain the origins of the hermitage appearing on the horizon.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे सप्तविंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The history of Siddhāśrama and the Vāmana avatāra.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra identifies the forest as Siddhāśrama, where Viṣṇu performed penance as the dwarf Vāmana. When Bali seized the three worlds, Viṣṇu was born to Aditi and approached Bali’s sacrifice. He requested three paces of land and reclaimed the universe for Mahendra. The sage returns to this site and asks Rāma to protect his upcoming sacrifice from rākṣasa interference. After receiving hospitality from ascetics, Viśvāmitra enters a state of dīkṣā.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे अष्टाविंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Rāma protects the sacrifice and defeats Subāhu.
chapters.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa guard the sacrificial ground for six nights. As the ritual concludes, the rākṣasas Mārīca and Subāhu appear like dark clouds to rain blood upon the altar. Rāma strikes Mārīca with the mānavāstra, hurling him into the ocean, and kills Subāhu using the āgneyāstra. He clears the remaining attackers with the vāyavyāstra. With the forest secured, Viśvāmitra completes the sacrifice and commends the princes for fulfilling their duty.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकोनत्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The sages travel toward Mithilā.
chapters.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa complete their morning rites and request new instructions from Viśvāmitra. The sages invite the brothers to King Janaka’s sacrifice in Mithilā to see a divine bow. After circling the Siddhāśrama, Viśvāmitra leads a caravan north toward the mountains. They halt at the banks of the Śoṇā river for evening prayers. Seeing the dense woods, Rāma asks the sage to explain the history of the land.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे त्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Vāyu disfigures the daughters of Kuśanābha.
chapters.es: Kuśa's four sons build the cities of Kauśāmbī, Mahodaya, Dharmāraṇya, and Girivraja. The river Sumāgadhī winds through the mountains of Vasumatī. Kuśanābha's one hundred daughters play in a garden. When the wind-god Vāyu demands they become his wives, the sisters refuse, deferring to their father’s authority. Angered by their rejection, Vāyu enters their bodies and bends their limbs, turning them into hunchbacks. The maidens return to the palace, where their father finds them disfigured.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकत्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The daughters of Kuśanābha marry Brahmadatta.
chapters.es: Kuśanābha praises his daughters for their kṣamā after they resist Vāyu. To resolve their plight, the king marries them to Brahmadatta, the mind-born son of the ascetic Cūli and the gandharvī Somadā. During the wedding ceremony, Brahmadatta takes their hands in marriage according to tradition. Upon this physical contact, the maidens lose their hunched backs and regain their natural forms. Kuśanābha sends the brides to Kāmpilya with their husband and his mother.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra describes his lineage and the Kauśikī river.
chapters.es: Kuśanābha performs a sacrifice to beget a son, Gādhi. Gādhi’s son, Viśvāmitra, recounts how his sister Satyavatī followed her husband in death and transformed into the Kauśikī river flowing from the Himavat. After explaining his lineage and his residence near her waters, Viśvāmitra describes the arrival of midnight. He points to the moon and the nocturnal creatures. Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa listen to his words before settling into sleep under the starlit sky.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे त्रयस्त्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra relates the origins of the Gaṅgā.
chapters.es: After morning rituals by the Śoṇā, Viśvāmitra leads Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa toward the Gaṅgā. They bathe in the water and offer oblations to ancestors before lighting sacrificial fires. Rāma asks about the river’s origin. Viśvāmitra explains how the mountain king Himavān and Menā fathered two daughters, Gaṅgā and Umā. While the gods took the elder daughter to the heavens to benefit the three worlds, Umā performed penance and became the wife of Rudra.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The gods receive Umā’s curse.
chapters.es: Śiva and Umā remain in union for a century until the gods, fearing the power of a divine son, intervene. Śiva agrees to retain his tejas, but his spilled energy pervades the earth, transforming into a white mountain and the reed forest where Kārtikeya is born. Angered by this interruption, Umā curses the gods with childlessness and the earth with many masters. Afterward, Śiva and Umā retreat to the peaks of the Himavat to perform penance.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे पञ्चत्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The birth of the celestial commander Kārttikeya.
chapters.es: The gods seek a commander and approach Brahmā, who directs Agni to beget a son through Gaṅgā. Agni pervades the river with the energy of Śiva, but Gaṅgā deposits the burning embryo upon the slopes of Himavān. This discharge transforms the landscape into a golden forest, producing copper, iron, and lead. Six kṛttikā nymphs nurse the newborn, who develops six faces to drink their milk. Named Kārttikeya and Skanda, the child receives anointment as the general of the celestial army.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The sixty thousand sons of Sagara.
chapters.es: King Sagara and his wives, Keśinī and Sumati, perform austerities on Himavat to obtain heirs. The sage Bhṛgu grants a choice: one son to continue the lineage or sixty thousand offspring. Keśinī bears Asamañja, a cruel youth who drowns children in the Sarayū and faces banishment. Sumati produces a gourd yielding sixty thousand infants, nurtured in jars of ghṛta. Asamañja’s virtuous son Aṃśumān remains in the capital while Sagara begins a Vedic sacrifice with his priests.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Sagara's sons excavate the earth for the horse.
chapters.es: King Sagara initiates a sacrifice between the Himavān and Vindhya. During the ritual, Indra assumes a demonic form and steals the consecrated horse. At Sagara’s command, his sixty thousand sons scour the earth. They use their diamond-hard arms, lances, and ploughs to excavate the ground, digging sixty thousand yojanas deep into the netherworld. Their violent search slaughters subterranean creatures, prompting terrified gods and serpents to seek refuge with the creator, Brahmā.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे अष्टात्रिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Kapila consumes the sons of Sagara.
chapters.es: Brahmā reassures the gods that the sons of Sagara are destined for destruction. Following their father’s command, the brothers dig into the rasātala. They encounter the cosmic elephants Virūpākṣa, Mahāpadma, Saumanasa, and Bhadra supporting the earth on their heads. In the northeast, they find the horse grazing near the sage Kapila. As the brothers rush toward him with weapons, Kapila utters a wrathful sound, and the entire host is instantly reduced to piles of ash.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Aṃśumān retrieves the horse and finds the ashes.
chapters.es: Aṃśumān descends into the earth to retrieve the sacrificial horse and find his uncles. He receives encouragement from the diggaja elephants before discovering his uncles reduced to heaps of ashes. The eagle Suparṇa explains that only the celestial Gaṅgā can sanctify the remains. Aṃśumān returns the horse to King Sagara, who completes his sacrifice. The king reigns for thirty thousand years but dies without finding a way to bring the river down to earth.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Bhagīratha performs penance for the Gaṅgā.
chapters.es: Anśumān and his son Dilīpa rule the Ikṣvāku kingdom but die without liberating their ancestors. Dilīpa’s son, Bhagīratha, performs rigorous penance at Gokarṇa. Standing with upraised arms amidst the heat of four fires and the sun, he pleases Brahmā. The deity grants his request for the river Gaṅgā to descend and purify his ancestors' ashes. Brahmā warns that only Śiva can sustain the force of the falling waters and advises the king to secure his support.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Śiva cushions the descent of the Gaṅgā.
chapters.es: Bhagīratha balances on his big toe for a year until Śiva agrees to cushion the river's descent. Gaṅgā falls from the sky, wandering through Śiva’s jaṭā before flowing toward the earth. Deities gather in chariots to witness the white foam and churning currents. The water purifies those it touches, allowing cursed souls to return to the heavens. Bhagīratha then mounts his chariot and leads the river across the land, followed by gods, spirits, and aquatic life.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Bhagīratha purifies the sons of Sagara.
chapters.es: Bhagīratha leads the Gaṅgā into the lower regions of the earth. The river flows over the ashes of the sixty thousand sons of Sagara, sending them to heaven. Brahmā appears to the king, naming the river Bhāgīrathī and Tripathagā for her path through three worlds. Bhagīratha offers the salila rites to his ancestors and bathes in the sacred stream. Having fulfilled the vow his predecessors failed to achieve, the king returns to rule his city while the gods return to their realms.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra relates the churning of the ocean.
chapters.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa board a boat to reach the northern bank, arriving at the city of Viśālā. Viśvāmitra describes how the sons of Diti and Aditi once churned the kṣīroda for the nectar of immortality. They used the mountain Mandara as a rod and the serpent Vāsuki as a rope. From the waters emerged apsaras, the horse Uccaiḥśravas, and amṛta. After a war over the nectar, Indra defeats the sons of Diti to rule the worlds.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Indra divides the embryo of Diti.
chapters.es: Grieving her sons, Diti asks Kaśyapa for a child capable of slaying Indra. Kaśyapa grants her request on the condition that she maintains physical purity for a millennium. Indra arrives at Kuśaplavana to serve Diti, waiting for a lapse in her discipline. When Diti falls asleep in an improper posture, she becomes aśuci. Indra enters her womb and uses his vajra to divide the embryo into seven crying parts.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Indra creates the Maruts and Rāma visits Viśālā.
chapters.es: Diti requests that Indra transform her severed embryo into seven wind deities. Indra grants her wish, naming the children Maruts and assigning them to celestial realms and the four directions. After they depart, Viśvāmitra recounts the lineage of the city Viśālā. He traces its kings from the founder Viśāla to the current ruler, Sumati. Upon hearing of the group's arrival, Sumati greets Viśvāmitra and Rāma with traditional honors, offering hospitality before their journey to see Janaka.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The curse and invisibility of Ahalyā.
chapters.es: King Sumati greets Viśvāmitra and the princes before they journey toward Mithilā. Upon encountering a deserted āśrama, Rāma inquires about its history. Viśvāmitra recounts how the sage Gautama practiced austerities there with his wife Ahalyā. When Indra assumed the sage’s form to seduce her, Gautama returned and cursed the deity. He further condemned Ahalyā to remain invisible within the grove until Rāma’s arrival purifies her. Gautama then retired to the Himavat peaks.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Rāma purifies Ahalyā in Gautama's hermitage.
chapters.es: Indra, deprived of his virility by Gautama’s wrath, appeals to the gods for restoration. The pitṛs graft the testicles of a meṣa onto the sky-god, establishing a sacrificial custom. Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa then enter the hermitage where Ahalyā has remained hidden. At Rāma’s arrival, her visibility returns. The brothers touch her feet, and she offers them formal hospitality. Gautama reunites with his wife, and the princes set out for Mithilā.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे अष्टचत्वारिंशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: King Janaka welcomes the princes to Mithilā.
chapters.es: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Viśvāmitra arrive at King Janaka’s sacrificial enclosure, finding the grounds crowded with brāhmaṇas. Janaka and the priest Śatānanda welcome the sage with arghya offerings. Observing the two brothers, who carry bows and resemble the twin Aśvins, Janaka inquires about their lineage. Viśvāmitra identifies them as the sons of Daśaratha and explains their journey from the Siddhāśrama to Mithilā to view the king’s famous bow.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Śatānanda relates the history of Viśvāmitra.
chapters.es: Śatānanda, the son of Gautama, greets Rāma and asks if Ahalyā has been reunited with his father. Viśvāmitra confirms the restoration of the family. Śatānanda then describes Viśvāmitra’s origins as a powerful monarch born to Gādhi in the line of Kuśa. He recounts how the king traveled with a vast akṣauhiṇī army until he reached the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha, an assembly of forest-dwelling ascetics that resembled brahmaloka.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे पञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Vasiṣṭha hosts Viśvāmitra’s army.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra arrives at the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha and accepts a seat with offerings of fruits and roots. The men exchange news regarding the state of the kingdom’s army and the hermitage’s sacrificial fires. Vasiṣṭha offers to host the king’s entire retinue. After the king consents, the sage calls for the cow Śabalā. He instructs her to generate various foods containing the ṣaḍrasa, or six tastes, to provide a meal for the royal guests.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकपञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra attempts to acquire the cow Śabalā.
chapters.es: Śabalā produces a feast of honey, sugarcane, and rice for Viśvāmitra’s army. Satisfied, the king demands the cow in exchange for a hundred thousand cattle, claiming his royal right to the prize. Vasiṣṭha declines, explaining that the cow provides the havyam and kavyam necessary for his agnihotra and other rituals. Despite offers of gold chariots and millions of cows, the sage remains firm, declaring the animal to be the source of his religious duties.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे द्विपञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Śabalā produces an army to defeat Viśvāmitra.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra drags Śabalā away by force, but she breaks free and returns to Vasiṣṭha. The sage confesses he cannot oppose a king’s akṣauhiṇī with his own strength. Śabalā argues that brahmabala remains the greater power and requests permission to defend herself. At Vasiṣṭha’s word, she creates hundreds of Pahlava warriors. When Viśvāmitra strikes them down, she produces legions of Śakas and Yavanas who use swords and lances to dismantle the king’s entire army.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra attacks the hermitage of Vasiṣṭha.
chapters.es: Vasiṣṭha commands the cow to produce warriors who annihilate Viśvāmitra’s army. When the king’s hundred sons charge, Vasiṣṭha reduces them to ashes with a single huṃkāra. Defeated, Viśvāmitra retreats to the Himalayas to obtain weapons from Śiva. Granted mastery over dhanurveda, he returns and incinerates the hermitage. Vasiṣṭha comforts the fleeing disciples and raises his staff, resembling the fire of destruction, to confront the king.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The brahmadaṇḍa swallows Viśvāmitra’s celestial weapons.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra launches the āgneya weapon against Vasiṣṭha, who counters with his brahmadaṇḍa. The king hurls celestial arms, including the pāśupata and the brahmāstra, but the wooden staff swallows every projectile. As Vasiṣṭha absorbs the strikes, sparks erupt from his pores, alarming the gods. Seeing his weapons fail, Viśvāmitra admits that royal strength is no match for spiritual power. He abandons his arms to seek the status of a brāhmaṇa through penance.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Triśaṅku seeks to reach heaven alive.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra travels south to perform tapas, fathering four sons. After a millennium, Brahmā grants him the rank of rājarṣi. Dissatisfied, the sage resumes his austerities. Meanwhile, King Triśaṅku resolves to ascend to heaven in his physical body. When Vasiṣṭha refuses to officiate such a sacrifice, Triśaṅku journeys south to meet the preceptor’s hundred sons. He prostrates before them, pleading for the ritual aid denied to him by their father.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Triśaṅku is cursed and seeks Viśvāmitra’s aid.
chapters.es: Triśaṅku approaches the hundred sons of Vasiṣṭha to request a sacrifice. They refuse to override their father's command and curse the king when he vows to find another way. Triśaṅku transforms into a caṇḍāla, draped in iron ornaments and funeral wreaths. Deserted by his ministers, he travels to Viśvāmitra. He laments that destiny has thwarted his merit and begs the sage to use human effort to help him enter heaven in his physical body.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra prepares a sacrifice for Triśaṅku.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra offers refuge to Triśaṅku, who appears in the form of a caṇḍāla. The sage vows to perform a sacrifice that will transport the king to heaven in his physical body. When the sons of Vasiṣṭha and Mahodaya refuse to participate and insult the rite, Viśvāmitra curses them. The sons are transformed into muṣṭika outcasts, while Mahodaya becomes a niṣāda hunter. The sage then prepares to begin the ritual.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे अष्टपञ्चाशः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra creates a new southern heaven.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra organizes a sacrifice to send Triśaṅku to heaven. When the gods refuse the offerings, the sage uses his tapas to propel the king upward. Indra strikes the king down, but Viśvāmitra arrests his fall in mid-air. The sage creates new constellations in the southern sky and threatens to replace the gods. Eventually, the deities agree to let Triśaṅku remain among these new stars, where he hangs head-downward as an immortal.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Ambarīṣa buys Śunaḥśepa for his sacrifice.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra moves to the western lake Puṣkara to resume his tapas. Meanwhile, Indra steals the sacrificial animal from King Ambarīṣa’s ritual. To complete the rite, the king offers a hundred thousand cows to the sage Ṛcīka for a son. The father refuses to part with the eldest and the mother protects the youngest. Consequently, the middle son Śunaḥśepa offers himself as the victim. Ambarīṣa places the boy on his chariot and departs to finish the sacrifice.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra saves Śunaḥśepha with sacred hymns.
chapters.es: King Ambarīṣa leads Śunaḥśepha toward the sacrifice, stopping at Puṣkara. Seeking life, the boy begs Viśvāmitra for protection. When the sage’s sons refuse to take the boy’s place, he curses them and teaches Śunaḥśepha two sacred gāthā hymns. Bound to the yūpa in red robes, Śunaḥśepha invokes Indra and Upendra. The gods grant the boy long life and bless the king’s ritual. Viśvāmitra then resumes his penance at the sacred lakes for a thousand years.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra continues his penance despite distractions.
chapters.es: Brahmā grants Viśvāmitra the status of ṛṣi after a thousand years of penance. The nymph Menakā then arrives at Puṣkara, distracting the ascetic for ten years. Recognizing this as a plot by the gods, he moves to the Kauśikī river to resume his vows. Brahmā later names him a maharṣi but notes his senses remain unconquered. Viśvāmitra responds by practicing pañcatapā among five fires. Perturbed by these extreme acts, Indra sends the nymph Rambhā to tempt him once more.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra curses the nymph Rambhā.
chapters.es: Indra commands the apsaras Rambhā to seduce Viśvāmitra and disrupt his austerities. Fearing the sage’s wrath, she obeys. When Viśvāmitra recognizes the deception, he curses her to remain a stone for ten thousand years, decreeing that a brāhmaṇa will eventually liberate her. Though the curse takes effect, Viśvāmitra suffers remorse, realizing his anger has once again depleted his accumulated tapas.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Viśvāmitra achieves the rank of brahmarṣi.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra travels to the eastern quarter and observes a vow of silence for a thousand years. He remains motionless like wood, refusing to yield to anger. His ascetic power disturbs the gods and causes the earth to tremble. Brahmā and the deities grant him the rank of brahmarṣi. Viśvāmitra requests formal recognition from his rival Vasiṣṭha, who acknowledges his new status. King Janaka concludes the assembly by praising the sage.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे चतुःषष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Janaka describes the bow and the birth of Sītā.
chapters.es: Janaka welcomes Viśvāmitra and the princes to Mithilā, where he recounts the history of a massive bow. Entrusted to his ancestors by the gods, the weapon once belonged to Rudra. Janaka describes finding his daughter Sītā in a furrow while ploughing a sacrificial field. He establishes her marriage price as a test of vīrya, or prowess. After many kings failed to lift the bow, Janaka offers to show the weapon to Rāma.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Rāma breaks the bow and wins Sītā.
chapters.es: Five thousand men haul an iron casket containing an ancient bow into the court. Following Viśvāmitra’s instruction, Rāma lifts the weapon and strings it. The frame snaps in two with a sound like a thunderclap, shaking the earth. Fulfilling the vow of vīryaśulkā, King Janaka declares Rāma the husband for Sītā. Messengers depart for Ayodhyā to invite King Daśaratha to Mithilā for the wedding.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Janaka invites Daśaratha to Mithilā.
chapters.es: Messengers from Mithilā arrive in Ayodhyā and inform Daśaratha that Rāma broke the divine bow. By this feat of vīryaśulkā, Rāma has won Sītā. Janaka requests the king’s presence to fulfill his vow. After consulting his advisors and Vasiṣṭha, Daśaratha accepts the proposal. He commands his ministers to prepare for the journey, planning to depart for Janaka’s capital with his priests and retinue the following morning.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha arrives in Videha.
chapters.es: Daśaratha commands his treasury officers and four-division army to depart for Videha. Sages led by Vasiṣṭha accompany the king's chariot. After four days, Janaka welcomes the party to his capital. He proposes the marriage ceremony follow the completion of his sacrifice. Daśaratha accepts Janaka’s hospitality and reunites with his sons, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. The assembled kings and sages spend the night in mutual honor.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे अष्टषष्टितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Vasiṣṭha recites the Ikṣvāku lineage.
chapters.es: Janaka summons his brother Kuśadhvaja from the banks of the Ikṣumatī river. When the kings and priests assemble, Daśaratha requests Vasiṣṭha to recount their family history. Vasiṣṭha traces the Ikṣvāku lineage from the creator Brahmā through ancestors like Sagara, Bhagīratha, and Raghu. This oral record confirms the standing of the solar dynasty. Finally, Vasiṣṭha formally asks Janaka for his daughters’ hands on behalf of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकोनसप्ततितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Janaka recites his ancestry and promises his daughters.
chapters.es: Janaka traces his lineage from Nimi and Mithi to his father Hrasvaromā. He recounts his victory over Sudhanvā, who had besieged the city to claim the bow of Śiva and the maiden Sītā. Having installed Kuśadhvaja as the ruler of Sāṅkāśya, Janaka formally offers Sītā to Rāma and Urmilā to Lakṣmaṇa. He requests Daśaratha to perform godāna rites before the wedding ceremony occurs under the Uttara-phālgunī nakṣatra.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे सप्ततितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha performs the godāna ceremony.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha propose that the daughters of Kuśadhvaja marry Bharata and Śatrughna. Janaka agrees, scheduling a joint ceremony when the Phalguni stars are favorable. Daśaratha returns to his quarters to perform śrāddha rites. The following morning, he conducts the godāna ceremony, gifting four hundred thousand gold-horned cows to the brāhmaṇas. The king stands among his sons, resembling the creator Prajāpati.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे एकसप्ततितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The four princes marry the daughters of Janaka.
chapters.es: Yudhajit arrives from Kekaya as Daśaratha completes the godāna. Adorned in jewels and led by Vasiṣṭha, the four princes enter the pavilion where Janaka waits. Janaka presents Sītā to Rāma as his sahadharmacarī, instructing him to take her hand. Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, and Śatrughna similarly take the hands of Urmilā, Māṇḍavī, and Śrutakīrti. The couples circumambulate the sacred fire and the sages as flowers fall from the sky.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे द्विसप्ततितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha encounters Jamadagnya Rāma.
chapters.es: Viśvāmitra departs for the mountains while Daśaratha leads the procession toward Ayodhyā. On the road, the cries of birds signal mixed omens. A violent storm soon blankets the earth in dust. From the darkness, the axe-wielding Jamadagnya Rāma emerges. Fearing he intends to slaughter the kṣatriya class, the sages offer him arghya as he confronts the young Rāma.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे त्रिसप्ततितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Paraśurāma challenges Rāma to a contest.
chapters.es: Paraśurāma halts the royal procession to challenge Rāma. While Daśaratha begs for his son’s safety, the ascetic explains the history of two celestial bows. He recounts an ancient contest where Viṣṇu overpowered Śiva, proving the strength of the vaiṣṇava bow now in his possession. After describing his legacy, Paraśurāma presents the weapon. He demands that Rāma string the bow and fix an arrow as a test of his strength.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे चतुःसप्ततितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: Rāma defeats Paraśurāma and destroys his merit.
chapters.es: Rāma seizes the vaiṣṇava bow from Paraśurāma and fixes a celestial arrow. Respecting Paraśurāma’s lineage, Rāma spares his life but offers to strike down either his mobility or his ascetic merit. Paraśurāma recognizes Rāma as Viṣṇu. He requests the destruction of his heavenly realms to keep his ability to reach Mount Mahendra. Rāma releases the arrow, clearing the sky. Paraśurāma circumambulates Rāma and departs for the mountain.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे पञ्चसप्ततितमः सर्गः

chapters.subtitle: The princes return to Ayodhyā with their brides.
chapters.es: Rāma delivers the bow to Varuṇa and reassures Daśaratha before the army enters Ayodhyā. Citizens decorate the streets with banners and flowers to welcome the returning princes. The queens receive the brides, who offer worship at family shrines. While the brothers serve their father, Rāma dwells with Sītā through the changing seasons. Together, the couple resembles Viṣṇu and the goddess Śrī.
chapters.name: बालकाण्डे षट्सप्ततितमः सर्गः
अयोध्याकाण्डे प्रथमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: King Daśaratha plans to name Rāma as successor.
chapters.es: Bharata and Śatrughna depart for Kekaya with their uncle Yudhājit. In Ayodhyā, Rāma serves his father and the public, handling administrative tasks with restraint. He masters the dhanurveda and studies dharma alongside the wise. King Daśaratha observes these qualities and resolves to appoint his son as yuvarāja. To initiate this transition, he convenes an assembly of kings and provincial leaders, seating them in a formal council to discuss the succession.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The assembly approves Daśaratha's plan to crown Rāma.
chapters.es: Daśaratha addresses the royal assembly, declaring his body weary from thousands of years under the white parasol. He proposes Rāma as yauvarāja. The gathered kings and citizens rejoice like peacocks at the arrival of rain. They describe how Rāma inquires after their families and rituals like a father. The assembly requests the immediate coronation of the prince, noting his mastery of weapons and his devotion to the welfare of all beings.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे तृतीयः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: King Daśaratha prepares for the coronation.
chapters.es: Daśaratha agrees to the request for Rāma’s coronation and commands the priests Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva to prepare the ceremony during the month of Caitra. Sumantra fetches Rāma by chariot to the assembly. After Rāma bows at his father’s feet, the king seats him on a golden throne and advises him to remain humble and control his senses. Rāma returns home while Kauśalyā rewards the messengers and the citizens worship their deities in celebration.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha schedules the coronation for the next day.
chapters.es: Daśaratha summons Rāma to announce that the royal consecration will occur the following day under the puṣya constellation. Citing his old age and alarming omens, the king urges a quick ceremony while Bharata remains away. He instructs Rāma and Sītā to fast and sleep on darbha grass. Rāma carries the news to Kauśalyā, who is meditating on Janārdana, and invites Lakṣmaṇa to share the kingdom's governance.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Vasiṣṭha instructs Rāma to perform ritual fasting.
chapters.es: At King Daśaratha’s request, the priest Vasiṣṭha travels to Rāma’s residence. Rāma receives him with honor and, alongside Sītā, performs a ritual fast and recites mantras for the yauvarājya installation. Outside, the streets of Ayodhyā are decorated with flags as crowds gather. Vasiṣṭha returns to report his success. Finally, the king dismisses his assembly and retires to the antaḥpura.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma prepares for coronation while the city celebrates.
chapters.es: Rāma bathes and offers havis into the sacred fire to worship Nārāyaṇa. Alongside Sītā, he observes a vow of silence and sleeps on a bed of kuśa grass. At dawn, he dons silk garments and performs morning rituals. Outside, citizens hang banners and arrange lamp-trees along the highways. The city fills with actors and dancers whose voices rise like the roar of the ocean as they praise the king and the approaching consecration.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Mantharā tells Kaikeyī about the coronation.
chapters.es: Mantharā ascends the palace and observes Ayodhyā’s streets strewn with lotus petals. Upon learning that Daśaratha intends to consecrate Rāma under the puṣya star, the hunchback rushes to Kaikeyī. She tells the queen that the king acts with deceit by sending Bharata away. Kaikeyī initially greets the news with joy. Seeing no difference between the two princes, she rewards her maid with a golden ornament for sharing the tidings.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Mantharā warns Kaikeyī of Bharata’s displacement.
chapters.es: Mantharā discards the gift and warns Kaikeyī that Rāma’s coronation will force her to serve Kauśalyā. Though Kaikeyī defends Rāma as a man of dharma, Mantharā insists that royal succession will sideline Bharata. She compares Rāma to a lion preying on an elephant and claims he will banish or kill his brother to ensure a thornless reign. She urges Kaikeyī to secure the kingdom for her son and exile Rāma.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे नवमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Kaikeyī prepares to demand Rāma's exile.
chapters.es: Mantharā reminds Kaikeyī of two boons King Daśaratha granted her. She instructs the queen to enter the krodhāgāra, cast off her ornaments, and demand Bharata’s coronation alongside Rāma’s fourteen-year exile. Kaikeyī praises the counsel and promises rewards. Stripping off her jewelry and silks, the queen lies upon the bare floor. She vows to remain there until the king grants her wishes.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे दशमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Kaikeyī demands Bharata’s coronation and Rāma’s exile.
chapters.es: Daśaratha enters the palace to find Kaikeyī lying on the floor. To soothe her, the king swears to grant whatever she desires. Invoking the deities as witnesses, Kaikeyī claims her two boons: the consecration of Bharata and the fourteen-year exile of Rāma to the Daṇḍaka forest. Wearing matted hair and bark, Rāma must live as an ascetic. Overcome by grief, Daśaratha falls to the earth and pleads with her to retract these demands.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकादशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha pleads with Kaikeyī and falls unconscious.
chapters.es: King Daśaratha lies on the floor, likened to the fallen king Yayāti. Kaikeyī reminds him of his promise and demands the exile of Rāma. The king reacts with anger and delirium, foreseeing his own death and public disgrace. As the sun sets, Daśaratha remains in darkness, pleading with folded hands for mercy. He begs for the night to end or for morning never to come. Despite his wailing, Kaikeyī remains unmoved, and the king falls unconscious.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे द्वादशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Kaikeyī forces the king to summon Rāma.
chapters.es: Kaikeyī urges the king to honor his boons, citing the sacrifices of Śaibya and Alarka. Prostrate on the floor, Daśaratha trembles like a bullock under a yoke. He compares his plight to Bali trapped by the noose of Indra. Though he disowns Kaikeyī and her son, he remains bound by the cord of dharma. At Kaikeyī’s command, the charioteer Sumantra departs to summon Rāma, unaware of the king's grief.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रयोदशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Officials gather as Sumantra fetches Rāma.
chapters.es: At daybreak under the puṣya star, priests and ministers gather for the royal consecration. Gold vessels filled with water from the Gaṅgā and Yamunā stand ready alongside vālavyajana fans. Sumantra enters the inner apartments to wake King Daśaratha, who commands him to fetch Rāma immediately. Passing through streets adorned with banners, Sumantra reaches Rāma’s palace and delivers the king’s message.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुर्दशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma leaves for the palace to meet the king.
chapters.es: Sumantra enters the inner apartments and finds Rāma seated with Sītā on a golden couch. Sumantra delivers Daśaratha’s summons, which Rāma interprets as a call for his abhiṣecana. After bidding farewell to Sītā, Rāma mounts a chariot accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, who holds the royal umbrella and cāmara. As the chariot rolls through the streets, the citizens of Ayodhyā gather to offer blessings and praise the heir.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चदशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma travels through the city to the palace.
chapters.es: Rāma rides his chariot through Ayodhyā, where the air carries the scent of agaru. Citizens crowd the highway to offer blessings, hoping for a reign that equals those of his ancestors. Rāma greets them according to their status, remaining steady despite their praise. Upon reaching the palace, he crosses the courtyards and enters the inner apartments. The gathered people remain outside, watching for his return like the ocean waiting for the moon.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे षोडशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma accepts exile to uphold his father's vow.
chapters.es: Rāma beholds Daśaratha weeping on a couch beside Kaikeyī. When the king fails to speak, Kaikeyī demands Rāma depart for the Daṇḍaka forest for fourteen years to fulfill a royal vow, allowing Bharata to rule. Rāma accepts the decree instantly to preserve his father’s honor. After Daśaratha faints, Rāma circumambulates the king and the golden consecration vessels. He maintains a steady composure while leaving the palace, followed by Lakṣmaṇa.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तदशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma tells Kauśalyā of his fourteen-year exile.
chapters.es: Rāma walks through the courtyards to reach his mother’s quarters. He finds Kauśalyā offering oblations to Agni for his welfare. After her greeting, Rāma announces his fourteen-year exile to the Daṇḍaka forest and Bharata’s upcoming coronation. Kauśalyā falls to the ground like a severed plantain tree. She laments her misfortune, comparing her enduring heart to iron and her past rituals to seeds sown in barren soil.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टादशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma explains his adherence to paternal orders.
chapters.es: Kauśalyā laments the exile while Lakṣmaṇa offers to seize the throne by force. Rāma rejects this violence, citing Paraśurāma and the sons of Sagara who followed paternal commands. He declines his mother’s plea to stay and her threat to fast to death, choosing instead to uphold dharma. After urging Lakṣmaṇa to abandon his anger, Rāma circumambulates Kauśalyā and prepares for the Daṇḍaka forest.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma accepts his exile and cites destiny.
chapters.es: Rāma approaches Lakṣmaṇa to halt the coronation festivities. He orders the ritual preparations dismantled to ease Kaikeyī’s anxiety and safeguard his father’s word. Preparing to don matted locks and deerskin, Rāma attributes the sudden reversal to daiva, or destiny. He argues that no mortal can resist this unseen force. He urges his brother to abandon resentment, viewing their mother’s harshness as the work of fate rather than her character.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे विंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa argues against destiny and offers to fight.
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa rejects the power of daiva. He argues that only the timid rely on destiny, while the brave exert pauruṣa. Shaking his forearm like an elephant’s trunk, he vows to use his bow and sword to secure the throne by force. He offers to crush any opponent, including their father, to ensure the consecration. Despite this outburst, Rāma remains committed to his father's word.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma persuades Kauśalyā to serve the king.
chapters.es: Kauśalyā grieves as she imagines her son scavenging for roots and fruits in the wild. She compares herself to a cow trailing her calf and begs to accompany him. Rāma refuses, reminding her that a husband remains a woman’s primary daivatam. He urges her to serve the aging king to prevent his collapse from sorrow. Accepting his resolve to fulfill the exile, she prepares svastyayana rituals to ensure his protection.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे द्वाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Kauśalyā performs protective rituals for Rāma.
chapters.es: Kauśalyā performs the ācamana rite and offers garlands to the deities. She invokes the guardians of the world, celestial bodies, and the seasons to protect Rāma from the forest's beasts. After muttering prayers, she ties a viśalyakaraṇī herb to his arm as an amulet. She smells his head in blessing and embraces him. Following a final circumambulation, Rāma departs for Sītā's residence, radiant in his own resolve.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma explains his exile and gives Sītā instructions.
chapters.es: Rāma enters his own residence. Sītā, having completed her prayers, meets him and notices his pale face. Rāma reveals that Daśaratha must honor two boons granted to Kaikeyī, resulting in a fourteen-year exile to the Daṇḍaka forest. He instructs Sītā to remain in the palace, serve the elder queens, and perform religious vows under Bharata’s rule. He cautions her to avoid praising him or causing offense.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुर्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sītā argues to follow Rāma into the forest.
chapters.es: Sītā rejects Rāma’s request to stay behind, asserting that a wife shares her husband’s fate. She offers to walk before him to crush thorns and kuśa grass, finding more comfort in the pādacchāyā, or the shadow of his feet, than in palaces. She promises to subsist on roots and fruits while wandering through lotus ponds. Even as she vows to choose death over separation, Rāma attempts to dissuade her by describing the hardships of the wilderness.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma warns Sītā about the forest's hardships.
chapters.es: Rāma lists the physical hardships of the forest to dissuade Sītā. He describes the roars of lions and the necessity of sleeping on the bare earth upon beds of fallen leaves. He explains the rigors of wearing valkala bark clothing, maintaining jaṭā matted hair, and enduring constant hunger. Sharp kuśa grass, stinging insects, and serpents obstruct the wilderness paths. Despite these warnings, Sītā remains grieved by his instruction to stay.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे षड्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sītā insists on joining Rāma in his forest exile.
chapters.es: Sītā rejects Rāma’s warnings, claiming that affection transforms forest hardships into benefits. She recalls childhood prophecies from brāhmaṇa palmists who predicted her life in the wilderness. Citing tradition, she identifies her husband as her daivata and insists on accompanying him. She threatens to die by poison, fire, or water if left behind. Despite her tears falling to the ground, Rāma continues to describe the dangers to dissuade her.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sītā convinces Rāma to let her join his exile.
chapters.es: Sītā rebukes Rāma for his attempt to leave her in Ayodhyā, asserting her devotion with the example of Sāvitrī. She describes the harsh forest environment—thorny trees and dust—as soft as silk in his presence. Faced with her threat of suicide and her bitter tears, Rāma relents. He compares her company to his own reputation and commands her to distribute her jewelry and wealth to brāhmaṇas and the needy before their departure.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma allows Lakṣmaṇa to join him in exile.
chapters.es: Rāma asks Lakṣmaṇa to remain in Ayodhyā to guard their mothers against Kaikeyī. Lakṣmaṇa refuses, vowing to serve as a guide and gatherer while carrying a khanitra and piṭaka. He asserts that Kauśalyā’s resources are sufficient for her care. Rāma yields, directing him to fetch the ancestral weapons from the house of Vasiṣṭha. After Lakṣmaṇa returns with the bows and armor, Rāma begins distributing his riches to brāhmaṇas.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma distributes his wealth before leaving.
chapters.es: Rāma prepares for exile by distributing his wealth. He presents golden aṅgada and kuṇḍala to the sage Suyajña, while Sītā offers her jewelry. On Rāma’s instruction, Lakṣmaṇa grants gems, chariots, and cattle to various brāhmaṇa families and the counselor Citraratha. Rāma playfully challenges the impoverished Trijaṭa to hurl a wooden staff to claim a large herd of cows. Finally, Rāma provides for his servants and entrusts them with his palace.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma walks through Ayodhyā to see his father.
chapters.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa carry weapons draped in flower garlands as they walk through Ayodhyā with Sītā. Crowds pack the streets, forcing citizens onto rooftops to watch the prince travel on foot. Observers lament seeing Sītā exposed to the public and the elements. The people vow to abandon their homes and follow them, turning the forest into a city. Rāma remains calm amidst their cries. He reaches the palace and asks Sumantra to announce his arrival.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma asks his father for permission to leave.
chapters.es: Rāma arrives at the palace with Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā. King Daśaratha summons his wives to witness the departure, then collapses in grief. Rāma lifts his father and requests formal permission to enter the Daṇḍaka forest. Though the king urges Rāma to seize the throne by force to bypass Kaikeyī’s boons, Rāma refuses. He insists on upholding his father’s word, choosing the forest over the kingdom to ensure the king remains truthful and Bharata rules.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha tries to send the royal treasury with Rāma.
chapters.es: Daśaratha commands Sumantra to equip an army, merchants, and the royal treasury to follow Rāma. He intends for his son to hunt and perform yajña while living in the wild. Kaikeyī protests, arguing that Bharata should not inherit a depleted kingdom. She cites the banishment of Asamañja by King Sagara. The minister Siddhārtha retorts that Asamañja was a criminal. Stricken with sorrow, Daśaratha vows to follow Rāma into the forest himself.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रयस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma and Sītā put on bark robes for exile.
chapters.es: Rāma rejects the royal army and requests simple bark robes, a basket, and a spade. Kaikeyī provides the cīra garments in front of the court. Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa cast aside their fine clothes to dress as ascetics. Sītā stands confused until Rāma helps her fasten the bark over her silk dress. King Daśaratha rebukes Kaikeyī for this cruelty. Before departing, Rāma entreats his father to look after the grieving Kauśalyā.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma and Sītā prepare to depart for the forest.
chapters.es: Daśaratha collapses upon seeing Rāma in ascetic robes. The king orders Sumantra to prepare a chariot and provides Sītā with fine garments for her exile. Kauśalyā instructs Sītā on the dharma of a wife, and Sītā compares a woman without a husband to a stringless vīṇā. Rāma consoles his mother and begs forgiveness from his stepmothers. The palace, once resonant with festive drums, now echoes with the loud wailing of the royal women.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma leaves for the forest in a chariot.
chapters.es: Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa circumambulate the king and bid farewell. Sumitrā instructs Lakṣmaṇa to serve Rāma as his father and the forest as Ayodhyā. They board a chariot equipped with weapons. As Sumantra drives, the citizens of Ayodhyā pursue the vehicle. Daśaratha and Kauśalyā follow on foot. Pained by his parents’ distress, Rāma commands Sumantra to hasten the horses, ignoring the king’s cries to stop, as the royal family watches.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Ayodhyā grieves as Rāma begins his journey.
chapters.es: Rāma departs with palms joined in salutation. In the harem, the queens wail like cows separated from their calves. King Daśaratha sinks into his seat, overwhelmed. The agnihotra fires go unlit while elephants and cows refuse fodder. In the sky, Mars and Jupiter crowd the moon, and the Viśākhā stars appear shrouded in smoke. Abandoning meals and family duties, the citizens weep in the streets. Ayodhyā trembles and groans, resembling the earth deprived of Indra.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha rejects Kaikeyī and returns to the city.
chapters.es: King Daśaratha watches the dust of the departing chariot until it vanishes. He rejects Kaikeyī’s touch, renouncing their marriage. Returning to a silent Ayodhyā, he retreats to Kauśalyā’s chambers, feeling the remorse of one who has slain a brāhmaṇa. He imagines Rāma sleeping on the forest floor, sighing like a bull elephant. Proclaiming that his eyesight has followed his son, the king lies on a couch and cries for the exiles.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Kauśalyā grieves and asks for Rāma’s return.
chapters.es: Kauśalyā addresses the exhausted king, likening Kaikeyī to a venomous serpent. She compares the king’s decision to a sacrificer giving the deities' portion to rākṣasa spirits. Kauśalyā asks when Ayodhyā will again rejoice with raised banners and showers of lāja upon her son's return. She attributes her misery to the actions of a past life where she might have hacked the udders of cows, comparing her state to a cow losing its calf.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sumitrā reassures Kauśalyā about Rāma’s safety.
chapters.es: Sumitrā comforts Kauśalyā by praising Rāma’s devotion to dharma and his father’s promise. She explains that nature will protect the exiles: the sun will not burn Rāma, and the moon will cool him. Armed with divine weapons from Viśvāmitra, Rāma travels with Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā toward a guaranteed return. Hearing these predictions of his eventual coronation and well-being, Kauśalyā’s sorrow disappears like a light cloud in the autumn sky.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The citizens of Ayodhyā follow Rāma into the forest.
chapters.es: Rāma drives toward the forest while the citizens follow his chariot in grief. He urges the crowd to transfer their loyalty to Bharata, describing his brother’s maturity. When elderly brāhmaṇas struggle to keep pace, Rāma alights from the chariot to walk beside them. These priests carry their vājapeya umbrellas to provide him shade. Even the birds and trees appear to plead for his return as the procession reaches the banks of the Tamasā river.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma secretly leaves his followers.
chapters.es: Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa camp on the banks of the Tamasā river. Rāma drinks only water and rests on a bed of leaves, while Lakṣmaṇa and Sumantra keep watch. At daybreak, Rāma observes the sleeping citizens who followed him. To spare them further hardship, he instructs Sumantra to drive the chariot in a deceptive path to hide their tracks. The trio crosses the river, leaving the grieving followers to return to Ayodhyā.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The people of Ayodhyā mourn Rāma's departure.
chapters.es: The citizens return home and find the city silent. Merchants abandon their stalls, and householders refuse to cook. In every house, women reproach their husbands for returning without Rāma. They envision the mountains and rivers of the wilderness offering hospitality to the exiles while they dread life under Kaikeyī. Comparing their state to animals delivered to a butcher, the people weep. They mourn the loss of the prince more than their own sons.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma leaves the kingdom and crosses several rivers.
chapters.es: Rāma travels through the night and reaches the border at dawn. Passing blooming forests and villages, he hears residents denounce Kaikeyī and the king. He crosses the Vedaśruti, Gomatī, and Syandikā rivers, pointing out ancestral Ikṣvāku lands to Sītā. While moving south, he tells the charioteer of his hope to return to the banks of the Sarayū river one day to hunt and reunite with his parents.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma meets Guha and rests by the river.
chapters.es: Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa reach Śṛṅgaverapura on the banks of the Gaṅgā and rest beneath an inguḍī tree. Guha, the king of the Niṣādas, welcomes Rāma with offerings of food. Adhering to his vow as a tāpasa, Rāma declines the royal comforts, accepting only fodder for his horses. He drinks only water and sleeps on the bare earth while Lakṣmaṇa and Guha keep watch with their bows until the night passes.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa guards Rāma and Sītā during the night.
chapters.es: Guha offers a bed to Lakṣmaṇa, yet the prince remains standing to guard Rāma and Sītā as they sleep on a bed of grass. Guha pledges his kinsmen’s protection, but Lakṣmaṇa finds sleep impossible while his brother lies on the earth. He laments the impending death of Daśaratha and the grief of his mothers, Kauśalyā and Sumitrā. Fearing for the fate of Ayodhyā, Lakṣmaṇa questions if they will ever return home. Guha weeps.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma crosses the Gaṅgā and enters the forest.
chapters.es: At dawn, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa fasten their quivers and walk toward the Gaṅgā. Rāma instructs Sumantra to return the chariot to Ayodhyā so Kaikeyī will know the exile has begun. The brothers apply nyagrodha latex to mat their hair into jaṭā and dress in bark garments. After crossing the river by boat, Sītā prays to the goddess for their safe return. The group enters the forest on foot and hunts for their evening meal.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma laments in the forest and Lakṣmaṇa consoles him.
chapters.es: After offering sandhyā prayers, Rāma rests on the earth for his first night in the forest. He fears that King Daśaratha, blinded by kāma, has prioritized passion over dharma and artha. Lamenting the potential suffering of Kauśalyā and Sumitrā under Kaikeyī’s rule, Rāma asks Lakṣmaṇa to return to the city. Lakṣmaṇa vows to remain. Rāma relents, permitting his brother to share the fourteen-year exile.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma meets Sage Bharadvāja at the river confluence.
chapters.es: Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa walk toward the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā. Guided by the sound of clashing waters and rising smoke, they reach the hermitage of Bharadvāja at Prayāga. Rāma introduces his family and explains their exile. The sage offers arghya and water, welcoming them to stay. Concerned about proximity to the city, Rāma requests a more secluded home. Bharadvāja directs them to Citrakūṭa mountain.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The exiles cross the Yamunā and find a campsite.
chapters.es: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Sītā leave the hermitage and reach the Kālindī river. The brothers lash together logs and bamboo to build a plava, covering it with uśīra grass. They ferry Sītā across the water and reach a large Śyāma banyan tree. Sītā circumambulates the tree in prayer, asking for a safe return to her family. After hunting deer for food, they walk deeper into the forest and select a campsite near the riverbank.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa build a hut at Citrakūṭa.
chapters.es: Rāma awakens Lakṣmaṇa at dawn to continue their journey toward Citrakūṭa. Along the path, he points out blooming kiṃśuka trees and heavy honeycombs. Upon reaching the mountain, Lakṣmaṇa constructs a parṇaśālā using timber and leaves. To sanctify the new dwelling, Lakṣmaṇa hunts and roasts a kṛṣṇamṛga while Rāma performs a ritual offering with sacred mantras. They settle into the leaf-covered hut near the Mālyavatī river.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sumantra returns to Ayodhyā and the king faints.
chapters.es: Sumantra returns to Ayodhyā after parting from Rāma at the Gaṅgā. He finds the city streets desolate and silent. Citizens throng the chariot, crying out when they learn the prince has crossed the river. Sumantra enters the royal palace to find King Daśaratha grieving in a white chamber. Upon hearing the messenger, the king falls unconscious to the floor. Kauśalyā lifts her husband while the women and citizens break into collective wailing.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे द्विपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sumantra tells the king news of the exiled family.
chapters.es: Daśaratha summons the charioteer Sumantra to hear news of his exiled children. The king sighs, asking how Rāma and Sītā survive on foot. Sumantra relays Rāma’s humble greetings and instructions for Bharata to honor all mothers equally. He recounts Lakṣmaṇa’s anger at the king’s decree and describes Sītā standing stunned and weeping. The report concludes with the image of Rāma supported by his brother’s arms as they watch the royal chariot depart.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sumantra returns and Daśaratha collapses.
chapters.es: Sumantra returns to Ayodhyā, where horses weep and citizens wail from their rooftops. Even the lotuses wither and forest animals fall silent in the absence of Rāma. Inside the palace, Daśaratha laments his decision to exile his son for the sake of Kaikeyī. He begs the charioteer to lead him to the forest, fearing his own death is imminent. Overwhelmed by the loss of the prince, the king calls out to Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa before collapsing.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sumantra tells Kauśalyā about the exiles' journey.
chapters.es: Kauśalyā collapses in grief, pleading with Sumantra to return her to the forest. The charioteer describes the exiles’ journey, reporting that Sītā remains cheerful. Her feet, though bare of alaktaka dye, shine like lotus buds. She ignores the wind and heat, feeling safe near Rāma despite the presence of lions and tigers. Lakṣmaṇa serves his brother as they subsist on wild fruits to uphold their father's vow. Kauśalyā continues to cry out for her son.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Kauśalyā blames King Daśaratha for Rāma's exile.
chapters.es: Kauśalyā weeps for Rāma and Sītā, questioning how they will endure wild grains and the roar of lions. She compares her son to a tiger that refuses food killed by another, asserting he will not reclaim a kingdom enjoyed by Bharata. Like used havis or kuśa grass, she deems the throne defiled. Likening the king to a fish that devours its own offspring, she laments her lost refuges until Daśaratha collapses under his grief.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha and Kauśalyā discuss their grief.
chapters.es: Daśaratha recalls his past sin of striking a hidden target by sound alone. Distressed by Rāma’s exile, he joins his hands in an añjali and begs Kauśalyā for mercy. Kauśalyā weeps, comparing her husband’s plea to a physical blow. She admits that śoka, or grief, has destroyed her fortitude and made the five days of exile feel like five years. As the sun sets, she offers consoling words to the king, who eventually finds sleep.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha recalls killing an ascetic boy.
chapters.es: Daśaratha wakes on the sixth night of the exile, attributing his current sorrow to a past deed. He describes a rainy night by the Sarayū river where, as a young śabdavedhī archer, he tracked sounds in the dark. Hearing a pitcher fill, he released a shaft thinking it was a wild elephant. Instead, he struck an ascetic youth. The boy lamented the fate of his blind, elderly parents before urging the king to remove the arrow.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Daśaratha describes a past curse and dies.
chapters.es: Daśaratha confesses to the blind forest-dwellers that he killed their son by mistaking his sound for an elephant. The grieving father directs the king to carry them to the riverbank, where they touch their son’s body before he ascends to heaven. The ascetic pronounces a śāpa that the king will die from sorrow over his own child. Recalling this curse while Rāma is in exile, Daśaratha laments his fate and breathes his last at midnight.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The household discovers Daśaratha’s death at dawn.
chapters.es: Bards and musicians gather at dawn to wake Daśaratha with songs. Attendants bring golden vessels of water and sandal paste. Entering the bedchamber, the maids find the king motionless and tremble like reeds in a stream. Their cries wake Kauśalyā and Sumitrā, who touch the body and collapse. Kauśalyā lies in the dust like a fallen star. The palace fills with the wails of the queens as they realize the king has died.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Ministers preserve King Daśaratha's body.
chapters.es: Kauśalyā cradles the king’s head and condemns Kaikeyī for the ruin of the Raghu lineage. She laments for the exiled Rāma and Sītā before attendants lead her away. To preserve the remains in the absence of his sons, ministers place Daśaratha in a tailadroṇī. Palace women wail and citizens gather in the streets to denounce Kaikeyī. Ayodhyā sits in darkness, resembling a sunless day or a starless night, as the people mourn their loss.

chapters.name: अयोध्याकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The assembly describes a kingless state.
chapters.es: Following sunrise, sages including Mārkaṇḍeya and Gautama gather with the priest Vasiṣṭha to address the empty throne. They describe a land without a king as a parched river or cattle wandering without a cowherd. In this state, clouds withhold rain and property vanishes.
