To steady her, he proposes the cremation of the king and the consecration of Aṅgada to the throne. Tārā rejects this counsel, asserting that a wife’s place remains with her husband even in death. She leaves the care of the kingdom to Sugrīva, staying by the fallen hero.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे द्वाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Vālin entrusts his kingdom to Sugrīva.
chapters.es: Breathing feebly, Vālin watches Sugrīva stand before the weeping Aṅgada. He blames fate for their conflict and asks Sugrīva to guard Aṅgada like a father. Vālin praises the wisdom of Tārā, urging his brother to follow her advice and serve Rāma. He transfers his divine golden mālā to Sugrīva, who accepts it in grief. Vālin instructs Aṅgada to remain loyal to the new king. As Vālin dies, Tārā collapses onto his body.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Nīla removes the arrow from Vālin.
chapters.es: Tārā embraces the fallen king, lamenting his preference for the soil. Blood and dust cover his limbs as Nīla pulls the glowing arrow from his chest. Red streams pour from the wound like minerals from a mountain. Tārā instructs Aṅgada to touch his father’s feet in final salutation. Even as life departs, a royal luster clings to the king, though the golden mālā gifted by Indra is no longer visible.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चतुर्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The monkeys perform Vālin’s funeral rites.
chapters.es: Rāma urges Sugrīva to accept the inevitability of kāla and fulfill his duty. Following Lakṣmaṇa’s instructions, the monkeys prepare a śibikā adorned with garlands and clothes. Sugrīva and Aṅgada carry Vālin toward the riverbank while scattering gems. After Tārā offers a final lament, Aṅgada places the body upon a sandalwood pyre and ignites the flames. The assembly then gathers at the water’s edge to offer libations for the departed king.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे पञ्चविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva is consecrated as King.
chapters.es: Sugrīva gathers with his ministers after funeral rites. Hanumān invites Rāma to enter the city, but Rāma declines to uphold the exile decree. He instructs the monkeys to crown Sugrīva and appoint Aṅgada as yuvarāja. While Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa retreat to a mountain cave for the rainy season, Sugrīva enters Kiṣkindhā. Leaders like Hanumān and Jāmbavān anoint him with consecrated waters from golden jars. Sugrīva regains his kingdom and his wife, Rumā.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे षड्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa dwell on Prasravaṇa.
chapters.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa dwell in a cave on the peak of Mount Prasravaṇa. The slopes echo with the roars of lions among thickets of vines and clear pools. Rāma spends nights grieving for his wife until Lakṣmaṇa encourages him to summon strength. Agreeing to set aside sorrow, Rāma waits through the prāvṛṣ rains. He remains on the mountain for four months, preparing to move against Rāvaṇa when the śarat season begins.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे सप्तविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma describes the monsoon at Mālyavān.
chapters.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa dwell on Mount Mālyavān as the monsoon begins. Dark clouds cover the sky, and lightning flashes, reminding Rāma of Sītā in the lap of Rāvaṇa. Peacocks dance and balākā birds fly in rows like white garlands. While the rain halts the expeditions of kings and scholars chant the Veda, Rāma suffers the pangs of separation. He decides to wait for autumn before asking Sugrīva to begin the search.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे अष्टाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān urges Sugrīva to aid Rāma.
chapters.es: The clear autumn sky reminds Rāma of his grief while Sugrīva remains distracted by palace life. Hanumān approaches the monkey king, urging him to repay his debt to his ally. He warns that a king who misses the season for action loses the merit of his deeds. Acknowledging his duty, Sugrīva orders Nīla to mobilize the monkey armies from every direction. He decrees that any leader failing to arrive within fifteen days will face death.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकोनत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma sends a warning to Sugrīva.
chapters.es: Autumn arrives with clear skies and the cries of cakravāka birds, sharpening Rāma’s grief. While the monsoon clouds retreat, Sugrīva remains immersed in pleasure, neglecting his promise. Rāma reminds Lakṣmaṇa that the rainy season has passed and the time for military expeditions has come. He commands his brother to enter Kiṣkindhā with a warning: the path of death taken by Vālin remains open for those who ignore their samaya.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa arrives at Kiṣkindhā in anger.
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa expresses fury at Sugrīva’s neglect. Rāma urges restraint, advising his brother to use gentle words. Wielding a bow resembling a mountain peak, Lakṣmaṇa strides toward Kiṣkindhā, crushing stones. His presence terrifies the monkey guards, who flee from his gaze. He stands at the gates like a five-headed serpent. Inside, ministers rouse Sugrīva, urging him to honor his pact and face the prince who waits at the entrance.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān advises Sugrīva to reconcile with Rāma.
chapters.es: Sugrīva gathers his counselors to address the arrival of Lakṣmaṇa. While the king maintains he has caused no offense, Hanumān identifies his neglect. He points to the flowering saptacchada trees and clear skies as signs that the season for campaigning has begun. Hanumān advises Sugrīva to abandon his distractions and seek reconciliation through an añjali greeting. This acknowledges Rāma’s role in slaying Vālin and reaffirms the monkey king’s commitment.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa enters Sugrīva’s inner palace.
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa enters the cave city of Kiṣkindhā, passing guards who retreat from his anger. He walks through streets lined with jewel-encrusted mansions, reaching the inner enclosures of the royal palace. Inside, the sound of tāntrī-gīta music fills the air. He finds Sugrīva seated upon a kāñcana-āsana beside his wife Rumā, surrounded by women. Witnessing this indulgence while Rāma waits, Lakṣmaṇa’s eyes redden with the intensity of Yama.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे त्रयस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa rebukes Sugrīva for his delay.
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa enters the inner palace, his face glowing with indignation over Rāma’s grief. Sugrīva springs from his golden throne to offer an añjali. Lakṣmaṇa condemns his indulgence in worldly pleasures. Citing ancient verses on the sin of ingratitude, Lakṣmaṇa warns the king that the path taken by the slain Vālin remains open for those who break their word. He demands immediate action in the search for Sītā.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Tārā pacifies Lakṣmaṇa’s anger.
chapters.es: Tārā approaches Lakṣmaṇa to defend Sugrīva’s loyalty. She explains that while the king was distracted by pleasures, like the ṛṣi Viśvāmitra with the apsaras Ghṛtācī, he remains grateful for Rāma’s help. She asserts that Sugrīva has already summoned the vānara hosts to confront the rākṣasa armies in Laṅkā. Tārā pledges the king’s life to the cause and urges Lakṣmaṇa to cool his anger, which terrifies the palace women.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे पञ्चत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva apologizes and pledges aid to Rāma.
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa accepts the words of Tārā, prompting Sugrīva to cast off his fear. The king credits his kingdom to Rāma’s grace. He recounts Rāma’s strength in piercing the sapta mahādrumāḥ with a single arrow and asks for pardon for his delay. Pleased, Lakṣmaṇa praises the king’s gratitude. He asks Sugrīva to depart at once to comfort the grieving Rāma and offers an apology for his own harsh words.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva summons the monkey hosts.
chapters.es: Sugrīva commands Hanumān to summon the monkey hosts from across the earth. Messengers travel to the peaks of Himavat and Vindhya, ordering leaders to arrive within ten days or face execution. Legions appearing like dark clouds gather in Kiṣkindhā. Some messengers retrieve medicinal auṣadha from an ancient sacrificial site of Maheśvara. They present these offerings to Sugrīva, reporting that the vast armies have assembled to serve his command.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva leads the assembled army to Rāma.
chapters.es: Sugrīva leaves his palace in a golden palanquin alongside Lakṣmaṇa. Accompanied by white umbrellas and the sound of conches, he travels to the forest to meet Rāma. Upon arrival, Sugrīva and his army prostrate before the prince. Rāma embraces him and provides counsel on balancing dharma, artha, and kāma. Sugrīva reports that millions of monkeys and bears are assembling to find Sītā. Seeing this, Rāma’s face brightens.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे अष्टात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The monkey leaders present their forces.
chapters.es: Rāma embraces Sugrīva, praising his loyalty. Immense clouds of dust blanket the sky as monkey hosts arrive from every quarter. Warriors such as Śatavali, Kesari, and Hanumān lead millions of followers with coats the color of gold and white clouds. The leaders offer salutations to Sugrīva, who presents the assembled vānara forces to Rāma. The troops then station themselves among mountain streams and forests to prepare for conflict.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva sends Vinata to the east.
chapters.es: Sugrīva presents his massive vānara army to Rāma and accepts command of the search. He orders the leader Vinata to march eastward with a hundred thousand monkeys. They must scour the banks of the Bhāgīrathī and Yamunā, the kingdoms of Magadha and Vaṅga, and Yavadvīpa. Sugrīva details landmarks like the Milky Ocean and the fiery vaḍavāmukha. The scouts have one month to locate Sītā or face execution.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva sends Aṅgada and Hanumān south.
chapters.es: Sugrīva dispatches a southern search party led by Aṅgada and Hanumān. He describes a route passing the Narmadā and Godāvarī, the Daṇḍaka forest, and the kingdoms of the Coḷas and Pāṇḍyas. The monkeys must visit Mount Malaya to honor Agastya before reaching the Pāṇḍya capital. Beyond the sea lies Rāvaṇa’s island. Sugrīva warns of the shadow-catching ogress Aṅgārakā and sets a one-month deadline for their return.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva sends Susheṇa to the west.
chapters.es: Sugrīva commands Susheṇa to lead monkey troops toward the western horizon. They search through the cities of Saurāṣṭra and Bāhlīka before reaching the confluence of the Sindhu and the ocean. The party must navigate the peaks of Hemagiri and avoid the fierce gandharva guardians of Pāriyātra. After exploring Mount Meru and the city of Prāgjyotiṣa, the monkeys must consult the sage Merusāvarṇi. Sugrīva sets a one-month deadline.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva sends Śatavali to the north.
chapters.es: Sugrīva sends Śatavali and a vast army to search the northern lands. They travel past the Kuru and Kāmboja tribes to reach the snowy Himavat. The search spans the peaks of Sudarśana and the desolation near Mount Kailāsa. After passing the hermitages of the Siddhas, the monkeys enter Uttarakuru, a region of golden lotuses. This expedition concludes at Somagiri, marking the limit of the known world where the sun no longer shines.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Rāma gives Hanumān his signet ring.
chapters.es: Sugrīva identifies Hanumān as the most capable messenger, comparing his speed to his father, Vāyu. Observing this trust, Rāma hands Hanumān a signet ring, or aṅgulīyam, inscribed with his name. This token allows Sītā to recognize Hanumān as a legitimate envoy. Hanumān places the ring on his forehead, bows at Rāma’s feet, and sets out. Leading the vānara army, he begins the search toward the south.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The monkey armies depart in four directions.
chapters.es: Following Sugrīva’s command, monkey armies spread across the earth. Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa remain on Prasravaṇa mountain to await the month’s deadline. Śatavali marches north, Vinata heads east, and Susheṇa travels west. Hanumān, Aṅgada, and Tāra depart for the south. The leaders vow to uproot trees, cleave the earth, and leap over a hundred yojana-s. They promise to kill Rāvaṇa and rescue Sītā as they gallop toward the horizons.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva explains his knowledge of geography.
chapters.es: Sugrīva recounts his journey across the earth to Rāma. After mistaking blood from a cave for the death of Vālin, Sugrīva blocked the entrance. Upon Vālin’s return, Sugrīva fled through every cardinal direction. He describes the world passing by like a whirling firebrand, an alātacakra. Guided by Hanumān, he took refuge on Mount Ṛṣyamūka, where a curse by the sage Mataṅga prevents Vālin from entering.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Scouts return after failing to find Sītā.
chapters.es: The vānara leaders depart in all directions, scouring mountains and riverbeds. They search through caves and thickets for a month. Vinata, Śatavali, and Susheṇa eventually return to Mount Prasravaṇa, reporting their unsuccessful efforts across the north, east, and west to Sugrīva and Rāma. Having explored every valley in their assigned quarters, they place their remaining hope in Hanumān, who travels the direction where Sītā was carried.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Aṅgada kills a demon in the forest.
chapters.es: Hanumān, Aṅgada, and Tāra lead the monkeys through the Vindhya caves. They enter a desolate forest cursed by the sage Kaṇḍu, where trees bear no fruit. In this landscape, they encounter a mountain-like demon. Mistaking him for Rāvaṇa, Aṅgada strikes the creature, killing him instantly. Despite their efforts, the search for Sītā remains unsuccessful, leaving the group exhausted as they prepare to move to another cave.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे अष्टचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Aṅgada leads the search in the Vindhyas.
chapters.es: Aṅgada gathers the exhausted search party in the Vindhya range. He warns of Sugrīva’s strict punishments and urges his companions to discard sleep. Supported by Gandhamādana, the monkeys climb a mountain to inspect groves of lodhra and saptaparṇa trees. Finding no sign of Sītā, they descend to the foothills. After resting briefly, Hanumān and the leaders resume their search through the southern caverns and forests.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Monkeys discover a golden city in a cave.
chapters.es: Hanumān leads the monkeys through the Vindhya range until they encounter a dark cave. Seeing swans emerging with wet wings, the group enters the tunnel. They walk a yojana through darkness before reaching a hidden grove of golden trees and palaces built of silver and gems. In this silent city filled with food, they find an ascetic woman dressed in deer skin. Hanumān greets the tāpasī and asks who owns these treasures.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Svayamprabhā hosts the monkeys in the cave.
chapters.es: The vānara-s enter a dark cave and discover a hidden city of gold. They encounter the ascetic Svayamprabhā clad in a kṛṣṇājina. She explains that the dānava Maya constructed these golden trees and jeweled palaces through māyā before Indra slew him. This realm now belongs to the apsaras Hemā. Svayamprabhā, the daughter of Merusāvarṇi, guards the site and offers the group food and water from the clear pools.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān recounts the mission to Svayamprabhā.
chapters.es: Hanumān recounts Rāma’s exile and Sītā’s abduction to the ascetic Svayamprabhā. He explains that Sugrīva dispatched the monkey host south to find the princess. After wandering exhausted, the monkeys followed birds into a dark grotto. Inside, they found sustenance provided by the ascetic’s hospitality. Having regained their strength, Hanumān offers to repay her, but she declines, stating that her commitment to dharma requires no service.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे द्विपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Monkeys exit the cave and fear Sugrīva.
chapters.es: Hanumān asks Svayamprabhā to lead the search party out of the magical cave. Using her power of tapas, she transports them to the coast while they cover their eyes. Realizing they have exceeded Sugrīva’s strict deadline, Aṅgada fears execution and proposes prāyopaveśana on the shore. Tāra suggests returning to the safety of the enchanted cave to hide from the monkey king’s wrath.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān dissuades Aṅgada from rebellion.
chapters.es: Hanumān observes Aṅgada’s intent to remain in the cave and employs bheda to divide the group. He warns Aṅgada that the monkeys will desert him for their families. He asserts that the shelter cannot withstand the arrows of Lakṣmaṇa. Finally, Hanumān advises Aṅgada to return to Sugrīva, arguing that the king is virtuous and will name his nephew as successor out of love for Tārā.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Aṅgada and the monkeys begin a fast.
chapters.es: Aṅgada rejects Sugrīva’s authority, citing the betrayal of Vālin. Fearing imprisonment, he spreads darbha grass upon the shore to begin prāyopaveśana. He sends respects to his mother Tārā and bids his companions return home. Refusing to leave, the vānara host sips water and sits together facing the east. Their collective wailing resounds through the coastal caves as they resolve to fast until death.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sampāti learns of Jaṭāyu’s death.
chapters.es: The monkeys prepare to fast to death when the vulture Sampāti emerges from a cave. Seeing them as food provided by destiny, he waits. Aṅgada laments their failure to find Sītā and mentions the sacrifice of Jaṭāyu. Shaken by the news of his brother’s death, Sampāti calls out to the monkeys. He asks for details of the fight in Janasthāna and explains how the sun’s rays burnt his wings, leaving him unable to move.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Aṅgada explains their mission to Sampāti.
chapters.es: Monkey leaders sit by the shore, prepared to die from fasting. When a large vulture appears, Aṅgada approaches and recounts the history of the monkey kings and Rāma’s exile into the Daṇḍaka forest. He describes Rāvaṇa’s abduction of Sītā and the death of the vulture Jaṭāyu. Aṅgada explains their alliance with Sugrīva and their despair at missing the search deadline, which led them to accept death on the seaside.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sampāti reveals Sītā’s location in Laṅkā.
chapters.es: Sampāti mourns Jaṭāyu and recounts how the sun scorched his wings. He assists the monkeys by describing how he saw Rāvaṇa carrying Sītā through the sky. He identifies Laṅkā, a city built by Viśvakarman, as her prison, located a hundred yojana-s across the southern sea. Using his vulture sight, he confirms Sītā remains confined in the harem. After the monkeys carry him to the shore to offer water to his brother, they find hope.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे अष्टपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sampāti recounts his son’s sighting of Rāvaṇa.
chapters.es: Jāmbavān and the monkeys gather around Sampāti to hear news of Sītā. Sampāti recounts how his son, Supārśva, blocked a mountain pass while hunting and encountered a dark figure carrying a radiant woman. This traveler requested passage with courtesy, and sages later identified him as Rāvaṇa. Though wingless, Sampāti urges the monkeys to act. He reminds them of their own power and the strength of the arrows of Rāma.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sampāti recalls meeting the sage Niśākara.
chapters.es: Sampāti bathes and offers water to Jaṭāyu before addressing the monkeys. He recounts falling to the mountain peaks long ago, his wings scorched by the sun. After eight thousand years of isolation, he sought out the sage Niśākara at a hermitage. The sage, followed by a procession of wild beasts, recognizes the featherless vulture. Niśākara questions Sampāti about his injuries and the loss of his flight.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sampāti describes the loss of his wings.
chapters.es: Sampāti recounts a competitive flight with Jaṭāyu to follow the sun from the peak of Kailāsa. As they ascend, the earth appears small. To save Jaṭāyu from the sun’s heat, Sampāti shields him with his wings. His own feathers burn, causing him to fall onto the Vindhya mountains. He loses his flight, while Jaṭāyu descends toward Janasthāna, leaving Sampāti disabled and longing for death.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Niśākara predicts Rāma’s arrival and the recovery.
chapters.es: The sage Niśākara comforts Sampāti with a prophecy. He describes the future exile of Rāma and the abduction of Sītā by Rāvaṇa. The sage predicts that Indra will provide celestial food to the captive Sītā, who will offer a portion to her husband. Niśākara instructs Sampāti to wait for the arrival of monkey messengers. By guiding these searchers, the bird will eventually regain his wings and his physical strength.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Sampāti regrows his wings and flies away.
chapters.es: After Niśākara enters his hermitage, Sampāti waits on the Vindhya range for over a century. He recalls his son’s failure to rescue Sītā but finds hope in the prophecy. While speaking to the monkeys, new red feathers—aruṇacchada—sprout. Sampāti regains his youthful strength and takes flight from the mountain peak. This restoration serves as a sign for the monkeys, who then travel south to find the daughter of Janaka.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Monkeys reach the ocean and Aṅgada calls volunteers.
chapters.es: Guided by Sampāti, the monkeys reach the shore of the southern ocean. The sight of churning water teeming with sea creatures fills the army with viṣāda. Aṅgada urges them to abandon this despondency, which saps a person’s tejas. The next morning, he challenges the leaders to leap the hundred yojana expanse. When the army remains silent, Aṅgada calls upon the warriors to declare their individual strength for the crossing.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे चतुःषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: The monkey leaders assess their leaping abilities.
chapters.es: The vānara leaders assess their strength, stating the distance in yojana units they can leap. The aged Jāmbavān recounts his youth when he circumambulated Viṣṇu during the trivikrama expansion, yet he now limits his reach to ninety. Prince Aṅgada volunteers for the hundred-yojana jump but expresses uncertainty regarding his return. Protecting the prince as the vital root of their mission, Jāmbavān declines his offer and turns to Hanumān.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Jāmbavān reminds Hanumān of his divine origin.
chapters.es: Jāmbavān approaches the silent Hanumān to recount the origins of his hidden power. He describes Hanumān’s birth to Añjanā and the wind-god Vāyu, recalling how the infant leaped toward the sun and survived a strike from Indra’s vajra. These events secured Hanumān boons of invulnerability. Citing his own age and previous feats during the strides of Viṣṇu, Jāmbavān urges Hanumān to leap across the ocean. Hanumān expands his body.

chapters.name: किष्किन्धाकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān prepares to leap from Mount Mahendra.
chapters.es: Hanumān expands his body until his face glows. He declares his lineage as the son of Vāyu and vows to cross the ocean, outstripping the speed of Garuḍa. After receiving blessings from Jāmbavān, he climbs Mount Mahendra. His weight crushes the stone peaks, causing water to gush and serpents to hiss. Fixing his mind on Sītā, he readies himself for the flight toward Laṅkā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे प्रथमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān expands his frame and launches from Mount Mahendra toward the south. His leap uproots trees and stirs the sea. During the flight, the golden mountain Maināka emerges from the waves to provide a resting place, which Hanumān acknowledges with a touch. He outmaneuvers the serpent Surasā through size-shifting and kills the demoness Siṃhikā by entering her mouth. Upon reaching the far shore, he shrinks his body and gazes at the city of Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān leaps across the ocean to Laṅkā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān stands upon Trikūṭa mountain, gazing at the walled city of Laṅkā. He observes golden gates, white mansions, and moats. Recognizing the strength of the rākṣasa guards, he concludes that a large army cannot take the city by force. He shrinks his frame to the size of a pṛṣadaṃśaka to slip past the sentries. As the moon rises like a white conch, he enters the city gates at dusk to search for Sītā.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān enters Laṅkā in a small form.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे तृतीयः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān enters Laṅkā at night and is challenged by the city's personified guardian. After he strikes her with his left fist, she recognizes him as the sign of the demons' downfall. He passes golden walls and gates inlaid with vaidūrya gems. He hears musical instruments and rākṣasas chanting Veda verses. He observes soldiers armed with tridents and bows. He reaches the royal palace grounds where four-tusked white elephants stand guard.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān defeats the city guardian and enters Laṅkā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān watches the moon rise over Laṅkā, comparing its radiance to a white bull. Below, the city stirs with music and nightly activity. He observes warriors drinking and reclining with their wives on palace terraces. He sees demonesses adorned in gold and jewels, yet none of these women is Sītā. Recalling her nature, he imagines her current state as a dust-covered streak of gold, leaving him dejected by his failed search.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān searches the city but cannot find Sītā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān searches the mansions of Laṅkā. He leaps between the dwellings of rākṣasa leaders, including Vibhīṣaṇa and Kumbhakarṇa, before entering the central palace of Rāvaṇa. He observes golden toraṇa arches, ivory-encrusted chariots, and war elephants. The air carries the scent of sandalwood and the sounds of mṛdaṅga drums. He passes through halls filled with gem-studded vessels and sleeping women, moving through the golden residence which rivals the mountain Mandara in scale.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān searches the mansions and Rāvaṇa’s palace.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān observes the golden lattices and weapon stores of the mansions in Laṅkā. He encounters the Puṣpaka chariot, an aerial vessel decorated with carvings of mountains and silver birds. The chariot features an image of the goddess Lakṣmī being bathed by elephants. Despite the wealth of gems and the work of the architect Maya, Hanumān continues to search the moonlit terraces and fragrant halls without finding Sītā.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān finds the Puṣpaka chariot in the palace.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān traverses the mansion of Rāvaṇa, reaching the Puṣpaka aerial chariot. Carved wolves and golden pillars support this vehicle. He enters a central hall filled with the scent of wine and incense. Thousands of women lie asleep on carpets, their limbs intertwined. They resemble a bed of lotuses or a cluster of fallen stars. Hanumān observes that while these women chose the king's company, the abducted Sītā remains absent from this luxury.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān observes the women in Rāvaṇa’s palace.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān enters a chamber where Rāvaṇa sleeps upon a golden dais. His arms, scarred by the tusks of Airāvata, rest like serpents beside his breathing frame. Surrounding him, exhausted women clutch vīṇā lutes and maḍḍuka drums. Hanumān observes the radiant Mandodarī. Mistaking her for Sītā due to her complexion, the messenger rejoices, leaping onto pillars and kissing his tail in a burst of simian joy.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān mistakes Mandodarī for Sītā in the palace.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे नवमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān moves through the banquet hall, observing women asleep on muraja drums. They rest amidst scattered golden vessels and portions of venison, buffalo, and poultry seasoned with salt. The air carries the scent of sandalwood and fermented mādhvīka wine. In the center, Rāvaṇa sleeps among his wives. Finding no trace of Jānakī, Hanumān reflects on the morality of entering the antaḥpura, concluding that his pure intention justifies the search.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān searches the banquet hall for Jānakī.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे दशमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān scours the palace grounds, searching through pavilions, galleries, and private chambers. Finding no trace of Sītā, he fears she has been killed. He dreads returning to the vānara army in failure. Invoking anirveda, the principle of perseverance, he resumes his quest. He opens every door and leaps over boundary walls, inspecting gardens. Though he sees many captive women, Sītā remains hidden, leaving him in renewed despondency.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān despairs and resolves to continue his search.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकादशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān leaps from an aerial chariot to the palace walls. He fears Sītā died of grief or fell into the sea. To return empty-handed would cause the deaths of Rāma and the vānara host. Rejecting suicide, he resolves to search the aśokavanikā. After offering salutations to Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and the vasus, he shrinks his body to enter the guarded grove and find the daughter of Janaka.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān decides to search the aśoka grove.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे द्वादशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān leaps into the palace groves, landing among flowering śāla and aśoka trees. His movement startles the birds and shakes the branches, covering him in blossoms until he resembles a mountain of flowers. He passes gem-paved ponds and artificial hills to reach a golden śiṃśapā tree. Climbing into its leaves, he waits for Sītā to arrive at the river for her evening sandhyā prayers, certain she will seek the solace of the woods.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān enters the grove and waits for Sītā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रयोदशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān watches from a śiṃśapā tree as the aśoka grove glows with dark trees. Amidst the flowering campaka and saptaparṇa, he discovers a white palace. There, a woman sits on the bare ground, emaciated and clad in a soiled yellow garment. Surrounded by rākṣasīs, she sighs like a serpent. Hanumān recognizes her as Sītā by matching her jewels, such as her karṇaveṣṭa, to Rāma’s earlier descriptions. He concludes that only mutual devotion keeps the couple alive.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān finds Sītā among the rākṣasī guards.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुर्दशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān watches Sītā from the branches, observing her golden skin dimmed by sorrow. He reflects on how Rāma defeated Vālin and Khara for her sake, noting her virtue outweighs the sovereignty of the three worlds. Sītā sits among rākṣasīs under an aśoka tree, resembling a frost-bitten lotus. Hanumān remains hidden in the śiṃśapā tree, certain that this grieving woman is the princess he seeks.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān recognizes Sītā as the wife of Rāma.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चदशः सर्गः
chapters.es: The moon rises like a swan swimming through blue water, cooling Hanumān with its rays. He spots Sītā in the aśokavanikā, encircled by rākṣasīs with animal faces and distorted limbs. Sītā sits like a boat heavy with sorrow, her hair unkempt and her clothes soiled with dust. Though she lacks ornaments, her devotion to Rāma remains evident. Overcome with joy, Hanumān sheds tears, bows to the princes in his heart, and settles within the branches.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān watches Sītā from the śiṃśapā tree.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे षोडशः सर्गः
chapters.es: At dawn, the sound of Vedic chanting by brahmarākṣasas fills the air as Rāvaṇa awakens. Driven by desire for Sītā, he enters the aśokavanikā followed by a hundred women bearing golden lamps and fans. Their jewelry clinks as they walk. From a leafy branch, Hanumān watches the king approach. Rāvaṇa wears a white robe and moves with a retinue like the moon among stars. Hanumān hides deeper in the foliage as the demon king nears Sītā.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa enters the grove at daybreak.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तदशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vaidehī trembles like a kadalī tree in a gale as Rāvaṇa approaches. She sits on the bare earth, covering her limbs with her arms. Her frame is emaciated from fasting, and she wears her hair in a single veṇī. She resembles a lotus pond trampled by elephants or a moon eclipsed by Rāhu. Though she appears like an extinguished flame, her mind remains fixed on Rāma, even as the demon king tries to allure and threaten her.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa approaches the grieving Sītā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टादशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa approaches Sītā as she sits on the bare earth, her hair tied in an ekaveṇī. He urges her to cast aside her soiled silk and adorn herself with sandalwood and gold. Boasting of triumphs over gods and demons, he offers her sovereignty over his harem and promises to gift lands to her father, Janaka. He dismisses Rāma as a powerless ascetic, comparing Sītā to moonlight hidden by clouds while demanding she choose luxury over grief.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa tempts Sītā with luxury and power.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकोनविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā places a blade of grass between herself and the demon king as a barrier. Recalling her birth, she rejects his advances and tells him to follow dharma. She warns that an immoral king ruins his country and predicts the destruction of Laṅkā. Comparing her devotion to the light of the sun, she advises him to seek peace with Rāma. She describes how Rāma’s arrows will soon fall to destroy the rākṣasas.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā rejects Rāvaṇa and warns him of Rāma.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे विंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa grants Sītā a two-month reprieve, demanding she submit or face death. Sītā remains defiant, likening the demon to a rabbit against Rāma’s strength as an elephant. She warns that her tapas could consume him, yet she awaits Rāma’s justice. Enraged, Rāvaṇa orders his rākṣasī guards to break her will using threats and persuasion. Finally, the demoness Dhanyamālinī coaxes the king back to his palace, leaving Sītā surrounded by her tormentors.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa gives Sītā a two-month deadline.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: After Rāvaṇa departs, a circle of rākṣasīs surrounds Sītā to pressure her. Ekajaṭā recounts the king’s lineage from the sage Pulastya and his father Viśravas. Other demonesses, including Harijaṭā and Vikaṭā, describe his military triumphs over the gods. They urge Sītā to abandon her husband for the wealth of the palace, reminding her that even the sun and wind obey the demon king’s will.
chapters.subtitle: rākṣasīs pressure Sītā to accept Rāvaṇa.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे द्वाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: rākṣasīs surround Sītā beneath a śiṃśapā tree, demanding she abandon Rāma for Rāvaṇa. They mock her devotion to a mortal and warn that her youth is fleeting. When she refuses, the rākṣasīs brandish axes. They threaten to tear out her heart and liver, while Śūrpaṇakhā calls for wine to celebrate a feast of human flesh. Trembling, Sītā clings to the tree as the hidden Hanumān watches his queen endure these terrors.
chapters.subtitle: rākṣasīs threaten to devour Sītā for her refusal.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Surrounded by rākṣasīs, Sītā weeps and rejects their demands. She clings to a flowering aśoka branch, her body trembling like a banana tree in a gale. Calling for Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, she laments that death remains out of reach despite her misery. Her braid sways like a serpent as she compares her life to a boat lost at sea. She curses the helplessness of her condition and her inability to end her life at will.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā weeps while surrounded by rākṣasīs.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुर्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā falls to the earth, weeping and tossing her body. She rejects the threats of the rākṣasīs and refuses to touch Rāvaṇa even with her left foot. Recalling Rāma’s victory over the demons of Janasthāna, she wonders why he has not arrived to rescue her. She predicts that his arrows will turn Laṅkā into a cemetery filled with funeral pyre smoke. Envying the equanimity of sages, she resolves to end her life rather than endure further separation.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā predicts the destruction of Laṅkā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: rākṣasīs threaten to devour Sītā until the elderly Trijatā describes a dream foretelling their destruction. She sees Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa wearing white garlands, riding a four-tusked elephant to reclaim Sītā. In contrast, Rāvaṇa falls from the Puṣpaka chariot with a shaven head and black clothing, dragged toward the south. Trijatā advises the guards to seek Sītā’s protection as physical signs appear: Sītā’s left eye and arm throb, signaling the end of her sorrow.
chapters.subtitle: Trijatā dreams of Rāma’s victory and Rāvaṇa’s fall.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे षड्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā trembles among the demonesses, comparing her terror to an elephant calf caught by a lion. Fearing Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa died pursuing a deceptive mṛga, she laments her futile devotion. Lacking poison or blades in the demon city, she approaches a flowering śiṃśapā tree. She grasps a branch and prepares to end her life, using her long veṇī as a noose to reach the lord of death.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā despairs and contemplates suicide.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā stands beneath the śiṃśapā tree as favorable nimitta appear. Her left eye throbs like a red lotus brushed by a fish, while her left arm and thigh tremble, foretelling a reunion with Rāma. Her golden clothing slips slightly as she stands. These physical signs revive her spirit like rain falling on a parched seed. Her face clears of grief, shining like the moon released from the mouth of Rāhu, as her exhaustion and fear dissolve into hope.
chapters.subtitle: Favorable omens appear to Sītā in the grove.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān watches Sītā from his hiding place, observing her grief and the threats of the guards. He weighs the risks of revealing himself, fearing that refined saṃskṛta might make her mistake him for Rāvaṇa. To avoid alerting the demon army, he decides to narrate the history of the Ikṣvāku dynasty. Hidden among the leaves, he begins to speak of Rāma’s virtues in a human tongue, seeking to win her trust through his words.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān plans a safe way to speak with Sītā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकोनत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān begins his narration by reciting the history of King Daśaratha and his son, Rāma. He describes the prince’s exile to the forest to honor his father’s word and the subsequent abduction of Jānakī by Rāvaṇa. Upon hearing these familiar details, the captive princess looks up into the śiṃśapā tree. She pushes aside her hair to find the minister of the monkey king, the son of the Wind-god, perched among the branches like the rising sun.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān narrates Rāma’s story to gain trust.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā discovers a white-clad vānara hidden within the tree branches. Startled, she questions if the encounter is a dream, fearing the inauspicious omens described in the śāstras regarding monkeys. She concludes that her persistent grief makes sleep impossible, suggesting the figure might be a hallucination born of her devotion to Rāma. However, seeing his tangible form and hearing his speech, she prays to Vācaspati and the gods that the creature’s words are true.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā sees Hanumān and fears it is a dream.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān approaches Sītā with palms joined in salutation. He asks if she is a goddess, noting her crumpled kauśeya and tears. Sītā identifies herself as the daughter of Janaka and the wife of Rāma. She recounts the lost coronation caused by Kaikeyī, the journey into the Daṇḍakāraṇya to preserve her father-in-law’s truth, and her abduction by Rāvaṇa. She concludes by stating she has only two months left to live.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān meets Sītā and she explains her exile.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān delivers news of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to the grieving Sītā. Though initially joyful, Sītā shrinks away, fearing the monkey is merely Rāvaṇa in disguise. Hanumān prostrates before her and recites the virtues of Rāma to calm her heart. He explains the alliance with the monkey king Sugrīva and his own journey across the ocean. By describing the coming defeat of the demons, he encourages her to set aside suspicion and trust his identity as a messenger.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān delivers news of Rāma to Sītā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रयस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā asks for the distinguishing marks of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. Hanumān describes Rāma as having lotus-petal eyes, a conch-shaped neck, and a dark complexion. He recounts the alliance with Sugrīva at mountain Ṛśyamūka and the recovery of Sītā’s dropped ornaments. He explains how the vulture Sampāti revealed her location in Laṅkā. After detailing his leap across the ocean and his birth as the son of Vāyu, Sītā sheds tears of joy and accepts him as a messenger.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān describes Rāma’s marks and their alliance.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān presents Rāma’s inscribed aṅgulīyakam to Sītā, who rejoices like the moon emerging from an eclipse. She questions the messenger about Rāma’s health, his military strategies, and his continued devotion. Hanumān describes Rāma’s ascetic life and mourning; the prince neglects food and sleep, calling her name in his dreams. Swearing by the Malaya and Meru mountains, Hanumān promises a rescue. Sītā finds comfort in these tidings, though she also grieves for her husband’s suffering.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān gives Sītā the signet ring.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā counts the two months remaining before Rāvaṇa’s deadline. When Hanumān offers to carry her across the ocean on his back, she doubts his small frame. The monkey expands his body until he resembles Mount Meru to demonstrate his strength. Sītā acknowledges his power but refuses the flight. She fears falling into the sea during an aerial battle and insists that Rāma must personally destroy the demons to uphold his honor and her vow to touch no other man.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān offers to rescue Sītā on his back.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān praises Sītā’s choice to stay and requests a token for Rāma. She recounts a private memory from Citrakūṭa, where Rāma used a blade of darbha grass as a brahmāstra to punish a persistent crow. Questioning why Rāma’s weapons remain silent against the demons, she unties her cūḍāmaṇi jewel and entrusts it to the messenger. Hanumān places the gem on his finger, circles her in respect, and prepares for his return flight across the ocean.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā gives Hanumān a jewel and a story.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā entrusts Hanumān with her cūḍāmaṇi jewel, a token Rāma will recognize. She urges the messenger to hasten her rescue but questions how an army can cross the vast ocean. Hanumān calms her doubts by describing the strength of the vānara host. He promises that Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa will soon arrive on his own back to destroy the city with their arrows. Reassured by these words, Sītā finally watches Hanumān prepare for his return flight.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān reassures Sītā about the vānara army.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā likens her relief to rain falling on thirsty crops. She gives Hanumān her cūḍāmaṇi hair-jewel and recounts private memories to share with Rāma: his painting a tilaka on her cheek with manaḥśilā and the blinding of a crow. She states she can survive only one more month in captivity. Hanumān assures her the Raghu princes will burn Laṅkā. After receiving her blessings for the army, Hanumān expands his body and prepares to leap back toward the north.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā sends her crest-jewel to Rāma.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān determines that only parākrama will subdue the demons, as diplomacy fails against those proud of their strength. To gauge the enemy's power before returning to Kiṣkindhā, he uproots the trees of the aśokavanikā with his thighs and levels its stone houses. He smashes mountain peaks, breaches ponds, and ruins the painted galleries. After devastating the landscape, the vānara stands at the main gateway, awaiting the demon army to begin combat.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān destroys the aśoka grove.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: rākṣasīs discover the ruined grove and question Sītā about the giant monkey. Sītā denies knowing him, observing that only a serpent knows a serpent’s tracks. Rāvaṇa sends eighty thousand kiṃkara demons to seize the intruder. Hanumān roars, strikes his tail, and assumes a mountain-like stature. He uproots an iron parigha from the gateway and kills the entire demon force. After the slaughter, he returns to the garden archway, waiting for Rāvaṇa to send more warriors.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān kills the kiṃkara demons.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān climbs the palace and assumes a massive form to roar across the city. He shouts his allegiance to Rāma and Sugrīva, identifying himself as a servant of the king of Kosala. When guards surround him, Hanumān uproots a gold-plated stambha from the building. He whirls the hundred-edged pillar to strike down a hundred attackers. From the sky, he warns the survivors that a vast army will soon arrive to destroy the city and its king.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān destroys the palace and warns the city.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Jambumālī arrives in a chariot drawn by donkeys to confront Hanumān at the city archway. The demon pierces the monkey with arrows, turning Hanumān’s face the color of a sun-struck lotus. When Jambumālī destroys a hurled rock and a śāla tree with his archery, Hanumān seizes an iron parigha. He whirls the weapon and strikes Jambumālī, crushing his body, chariot, and weapons into the earth. Hearing of this defeat, Rāvaṇa sends the sons of his ministers.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān kills the demon warrior Jambumālī.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Seven sons of ministers advance in chariots, raining arrows upon Hanumān at the toraṇa. The monkey leaps into the ambara to dodge the shafts. He strikes the warriors with his palms, feet, and fists, and uses his nails to pierce them. He crushes others against his chest and thighs. As the ministers’ sons fall, their horses and elephants collapse and the army scatters. Having defeated them, Hanumān returns to the archway to wait for the next assault.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān kills the seven sons of the ministers.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa dispatches five generals—Virūpākṣa, Yūpākṣa, Durdhara, Praghasa, and Bhāsakarṇa—warning that Hanumān is a divine being in monkey form. Hanumān waits at the toraṇa archway. He leaps from the sky to crush Durdhara’s chariot, then uproots a śāla tree to strike down Virūpākṣa and Yūpākṣa. Though wounded by spears, he hurls a mountain peak at Praghasa and Bhāsakarṇa. After dismantling the remaining cavalry, the blood-smeared vānara stands at the gate like the god of death.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān kills five rākṣasa generals.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Prince Akṣa ascends a golden chariot yoked with eight horses to confront Hanumān at the garden gate. He strikes the vānara with three sharp arrows. Hanumān admires the youth’s discipline but recognizes his growing power. He leaps into the sky, crushing the horses and chariot with his palms. As Akṣa flies upward, Hanumān seizes his feet. He whirls the prince repeatedly like Garuḍa seizing a serpent before dashing him against the ground, shattering his limbs. Hanumān then returns to the archway.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān defeats and kills Prince Akṣa.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa sends Indrajit to confront Hanumān. Mounted on a chariot yoked to four tigers, Indrajit discharges golden arrows that Hanumān evades by leaping through the air. Realizing the monkey’s strength, Indrajit binds him with the brahmāstra. Hanumān submits to the divine power but finds himself released when the demons wrap him in hemp ropes. Dragged into the assembly, Hanumān faces the ten-headed king and identifies himself as a messenger from the monkey lord.
chapters.subtitle: Indrajit captures Hanumān using the brahmāstra.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān stands before Rāvaṇa, who sits upon a crystal throne encrusted with gems. The king wears a golden crown and strings of pearls while his ten heads rise like the peaks of Mandara. His arms, smeared with red candana, resemble five-hooded serpents. Attendants wave whisks as ministers like Prahasta surround him. Hanumān observes the king’s radiance, noting that unrighteousness alone prevents him from ruling the gods. The dark-bodied king appears like a rain cloud resting on the summit of Mount Meru.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān observes Rāvaṇa in the royal assembly.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa commands Prahasta to question the captive. Prahasta asks if the intruder is a spy sent by Indra, Yama, or Viṣṇu. Hanumān denies divine alliance, identifying as a vānara. He explains that he destroyed the grove to force an audience with the king. Although the brahmāstra no longer binds him due to a boon from Brahmā, he remains in the palace to deliver a message. He declares himself a dūta of Rāma and urges the king to listen to his words.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān identifies himself as a messenger for Rāma.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān stands before Rāvaṇa as a messenger from Sugrīva. He recounts Rāma's exile and the loss of Sītā in the Daṇḍaka forest. After describing the alliance between the prince and the monkey king, Hanumān warns that holding Sītā is like harboring a venomous serpent or the dark night of dissolution, kālarātri. He urges the return of the captive to maintain dharma and avoid the fire of Rāma's anger. Insulted by this advice, Rāvaṇa orders the execution of the messenger.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān advises Rāvaṇa to return Sītā.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa orders the execution of Hanumān in a fit of rage. Vibhīṣaṇa intervenes, citing the dharma of kings which forbids the killing of a dūta. He argues that a messenger merely relays the words of others and suggests alternative punishments like flogging or shaving the head. By sparing the captive, Vibhīṣaṇa claims the news will reach the princes across the ocean, eventually drawing them into battle where the rākṣasa armies can prove their superiority.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa prevents the execution of Hanumān.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa accepts Vibhīṣaṇa's counsel and orders Hanumān’s tail set ablaze. Demons wrap the tail in oily rags, parading the bound vānara through Laṅkā's streets. Hanumān uses the march to map the city’s fortifications. In the aśokavana, Sītā prays for agni to remain cool, and the fire does not harm him. Hanumān shrinks to escape his bonds, regains his size, and kills his guards with an iron parigha before surveying the city from the gates.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa sets fire to Hanumān’s tail.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे द्विपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān decides to further torment the demons by setting their city ablaze. Using the fire on his tail, he leaps across palatial rooftops, turning the wind-swept flames into a fire that melts golden windows and precious gems. Molten silver, coral, and vaidūrya flow from the collapsing structures of Laṅkā. After reducing the mansions to ash and killing many more inhabitants, he contemplates Rāma and extinguishes his burning tail in the ocean.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān burns Laṅkā and douses his tail.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān surveys the smoking ruins of Laṅkā and fears that Sītā perished in the fire. He reproaches his impulsive anger, dreading that he has failed the Ikṣvāku princes. He soon reasons that the fire which spared his own tail would not harm a woman protected by her own tapas. After hearing celestial cāraṇas confirm her safety, his anxiety fades. Reassured by these omens, he resolves to see Jānakī once more before departing.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān confirms Sītā’s safety after the fire.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān salutes Jānakī under the śiṃśapā tree before his departure. Sītā urges him to ensure Rāma arrives with an army to reclaim her through valor. After reassuring her, Hanumān ascends Mount Ariṣṭa. He expands his body and leaps toward the north. The force of his feet crushes the stone and uproots blossoming trees. Disturbed snakes and Vidyādharī women flee as the mountain sinks into the earth, eventually lying level with the ground.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān leaps from Mount Ariṣṭa to return.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān flies across the sky, appearing and disappearing among clouds like the moon. He touches the Sunābha mountain and descends onto Mount Mahendra with a roar that alerts the waiting vānara host. Jāmbavān and Aṅgada lead the monkeys to welcome him with roots and fruits. Hanumān announces his success with the words dṛṣṭā devī and describes finding Sītā in an aśoka grove. The monkeys cheer and surround him on the mountain peak to hear the details of his journey.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān returns to Mount Mahendra.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān stands on the summit of Mount Mahendra and narrates his flight across the ocean. He describes passing the golden Maināka and outwitting the serpent-mother Surasā. After slaying the demoness Siṃhikā, he reaches Laṅkā and finds Sītā beneath a śiṃśapā tree. He recounts delivering the aṅgulīyaka ring, destroying the royal grove, and slaying Rāvaṇa’s sons. Finally, he explains how he burned the city with his own flaming tail and confirmed Sītā’s safety before leaping back.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān narrates his journey to the monkeys.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān recounts finding Sītā beneath a śiṃśapā tree in the aśoka grove. Surrounded by rākṣasīs, she wears a single dusty garment and an ekaveṇī braid. Though her tapas could incinerate Rāvaṇa, she remains devoted to Rāma. Hanumān gained her trust by describing the alliance with Sugrīva. Her own conduct preserves her while she waits for her husband to kill her captor. Hanumān urges the monkeys to act now, describing her grief and her firm refusal to submit.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān describes finding Sītā in the grove.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे अष्टपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Aṅgada addresses the gathered monkey leaders, arguing that returning to Rāma without Sītā is improper. He declares that his warriors can destroy the rākṣasa forces and shatter the city of Laṅkā. He cites the strength of the brothers Mainda and Dvivida, who possess celestial boons of invulnerability. While Aṅgada urges an immediate rescue to complete the mission, the elder Jāmbavān counsels restraint. He acknowledges their physical power but insists they must act according to Rāma’s specific command.
chapters.subtitle: Aṅgada proposes a rescue and Jāmbavān advises.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: The monkeys depart from Mahendra and descend into Madhuvanam, a restricted grove belonging to Sugrīva. After Jāmbavān and Aṅgada grant permission, the troop drinks the honey and becomes intoxicated. They sing, dance, and leap from branches, destroying the flowers and foliage. When the keeper Dadhimukha tries to stop the chaos with reprimands, the monkeys turn on him. They scratch his skin with nails, bite him, and kick him, completely looting the garden while ignoring the elder’s authority.
chapters.subtitle: The monkeys celebrate in the Madhuvanam grove.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān permits the vānara army to feast on the honey of Madhuvanam. The monkeys consume the honey, harass guards, and dance in their intoxication. When Dadhimukha, the garden’s keeper, attempts to stop the chaos with stones, Aṅgada strikes him down. Bleeding and defeated, Dadhimukha flies to where Sugrīva, Rāma, and Lakṣmaṇa are stationed. He lands and bows at Sugrīva’s feet, seeking redress for the destruction of the ancestral grove by the celebrating monkeys.
chapters.subtitle: Dadhimukha reports the grove’s destruction to Sugrīva.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Dadhimukha prostrates before Sugrīva to report the ruin of the Madhuvanam grove. He describes how the returning search party, led by Hanumān and Aṅgada, overran the guards to feast on honey. Sugrīva interprets this rowdy celebration as proof of success and assures Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa that Sītā has been found. The king pardons the monkeys for their trespass and requests their swift return, eager to hear Hanumān’s report of his deeds in the south.
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva interprets the celebration as success.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Dadhimukha offers salutations to Aṅgada and apologizes for his earlier opposition in the honey grove. Aṅgada accepts the apology and leads the vānara army through the sky toward Kiṣkindhā. Seeing their noisy approach, Sugrīva shakes his tail in joy and assures a grieving Rāma that Sītā has surely been found. The monkeys descend near the leaders. Hanumān bows his head and delivers the message that the goddess is safe and devoted. Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa recognize the completion of the mission.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān and the monkeys return to Rāma.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: The vānaras reach Prasravaṇa mountain to report their findings to Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Sugrīva. Hanumān recounts crossing the ocean to find Sītā imprisoned in Laṅkā. He describes her emaciated form and her single braid, or ekaveṇī, which she wears in grief. To prove his meeting, he shares the story of the crow at Citrakūṭa and presents her cūḍāmaṇi crest-jewel. Relieving the princes' anxiety, he relays Sītā’s vow to survive only one more month and urges them to cross the sea.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān delivers Sītā’s message and jewel.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुःषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma receives the cūḍāmaṇi from Hanumān and presses the jewel to his chest, weeping alongside Lakṣmaṇa. He compares his heart’s surge of emotion to a cow releasing milk for its calf. Identifying the gem as a gift from Indra to King Janaka, he feels the presence of his family within the stone. Rāma asks Hanumān to repeat Sītā’s message, likening her words to healing medicine. Overwhelmed by the sight of the ornament without his wife, he asks to be led immediately to her.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma receives Sītā’s jewel and weeps.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān conveys Sītā’s message to Rāma, recounting the time at Citrakūṭa when a crow injured her. He describes how Rāma launched a brahmāstra from a blade of darbha grass to punish the bird. Sītā questions why Rāma now hesitates to strike the rākṣasas and wonders if her sins cause his indifference. Hanumān reassures her of Rāma’s grief and approaching rescue. He presents the cūḍāmaṇi jewel as a token and reports her final plea for rescue from the ocean of sorrow.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān repeats Sītā’s message and the crow story.

chapters.name: सुन्दरकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā urges Hanumān to prompt Rāma to rescue her through open combat rather than stealth. She voices concerns over the vast ocean, questioning how the army or the princes can cross a barrier passable only by Vāyu, Garuḍa, or Hanumān himself. Hanumān reassures her, describing the strength of Sugrīva’s monkey forces and his own status as their least powerful member. He promises that Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa will soon arrive at the gates of Laṅkā riding upon his back to end her suffering.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān reassures Sītā of Rāma’s arrival.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे प्रथमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma listens to Hanumān’s report and commends his return from the guarded city of Laṅkā. He compares the leap across the ocean to the flight of Garuḍa and praises Hanumān for preserving the Raghu lineage by finding Sītā. Lacking other rewards, Rāma offers an embrace. The joy of the news quickly shifts to anxiety as Rāma considers the vast water. He stands troubled, questioning how the vānara army will reach the southern shore across the deep sea.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma praises Hanumān and questions the ocean crossing.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sugrīva counsels Rāma to set aside his grief and prepare for the march on Laṅkā. Since the location of Sītā is known, Sugrīva argues that despondency only hinders progress. He pledges the loyalty of the vānara army, describing them as warriors who change shape at will and fight with uprooted trees and stones. They plan to construct a setu across the ocean to reach Mount Trikūṭa. Sugrīva urges Rāma to replace sorrow with resolve.
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva encourages Rāma to resolve for war.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे तृतीयः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma questions Hanumān about the fortifications of Laṅkā. Hanumān recounts the massive gates secured by iron parigha and stone-throwing yantra engines. A golden prākāra wall stands above deep moats stocked with crocodiles. Mechanical drawbridges control access to the city, while Rāvaṇa constantly inspects his divisions of elephants and chariots. Millions of rākṣasa warriors guard the four gateways. Hanumān asserts that once the vānara host crosses the sea, the city’s destruction is certain.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān describes the fortifications of Laṅkā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma commands the vānara army to march south during an auspicious muhūrta. Riding upon Hanumān, he leads a massive host while Lakṣmaṇa follows on Aṅgada’s shoulders. Commanders like Nīla and Sugrīva organize the ranks as they traverse the Sahya and Malaya ranges. The monkeys forage for fruit and honey, their vast numbers raising clouds of dust. Upon reaching Mount Mahendra, the leaders survey the salt ocean and prepare to camp at the shore.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma leads the army to the southern ocean.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Nīla settles the vānara army on the northern ocean shore while Mainda and Dvivida patrol the perimeter. Rāma stands with Lakṣmaṇa and laments Sītā’s captivity, fearing the passage of time. He asks the wind to touch him after it has touched her and compares his survival to a dry field nourished by a nearby wet one. He envisions defeating the rākṣasa king to rescue her. As the sun sets, Rāma performs his sandhyā prayers.
chapters.subtitle: The army camps while Rāma laments for Sītā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa assembles his ministers in Laṅkā after Hanumān destroys the city’s defenses. Lowering his head, the king seeks a strategy against the approaching Rāma. He identifies mantra, or counsel, as the source of victory and classifies advisors into three grades based on their capacity for consensus. As the vānara army nears the shore, Rāvaṇa prompts his court to determine a course of action that protects the city before the enemy crosses the ocean.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa consults his ministers regarding the invasion.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः
chapters.es: The rākṣasa commanders remind Rāvaṇa of his history of conquest. They list his victory over Kubera at Mount Kailāsa and his defeat of the serpent kings Vāsuki and Takṣaka in the subterranean realms. They remind him that the architect Maya offered Mandodarī in marriage out of fear and that even the sons of Varuṇa and the forces of Yama fell before him. These generals urge their king to dismiss all concern regarding Rāma.
chapters.subtitle: Ministers remind Rāvaṇa of his previous conquests.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Prahastha offers to clear the earth of vānaras, dismissing Hanumān’s earlier infiltration. Following him, Durmukha vows to avenge the insult to Laṅkā’s royal quarters. Vajradaṃṣṭra brandishes a blood-stained iron bludgeon, promising to slay Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. Nikumbha and Vajrahanu urge the other rākṣasas to remain at ease and drink wine while they go forth alone to consume the enemy forces and crush the monkey host.
chapters.subtitle: Rākṣasa leaders vow to destroy the enemy.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे नवमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rākṣasa warriors brandish spears and bows, vowing to slay Rāma and the vānara army. Vibhīṣaṇa silences the assembly and urges Rāvaṇa to seek peace through sāma, dāna, and bheda before resorting to force. He cites Hanumān’s leap across the ocean as proof of the enemy’s strength. Identifying the abduction of Sītā as the cause of their peril, he pleads for the return of Maithilī to prevent the destruction of Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa advises the return of Sītā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे दशमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa rejects the counsel of Vibhīṣaṇa, labeling him a traitorous kinsman. He compares the danger of relatives to wild elephants betrayed by their own kind to hunters. Insulted and threatened, Vibhīṣaṇa rises into the sky with four companions. He warns that while flatterers are common, those who speak beneficial but unpleasant truths are rare. Predicting Rāvaṇa's death by the golden arrows of Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa abandons the city of Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa insults Vibhīṣaṇa and Vibhīṣaṇa departs.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकादशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa descends to the northern shore with four ministers, appearing like a lightning bolt above the vānara army. He identifies himself as the brother of Rāvaṇa and requests protection after failing to convince the king to release Sītā. Sugrīva suspects a ruse and calls for execution. Aṅgada and Jāmbavān advise caution. Hanumān observes the newcomer's clear speech and calm expression, noting that he seeks a kingdom after witnessing the coronation of Sugrīva.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa seeks refuge with Rāma's army.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्वादशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma addresses the vānara leaders regarding Vibhīṣaṇa’s request. He argues that a person seeking friendship must not be turned away. To illustrate this duty, he cites the legend of a dove providing hospitality to a fowler and the teachings of the sage Kaṇḍu. Rāma declares a formal vrata to grant safety, or abhaya, to any being who utters the words “I am yours.” He instructs Sugrīva to bring the refugee forward.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma vows to protect those seeking asylum.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रयोदशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa prostrates before Rāma and pledges his support against Rāvaṇa. Rāma embraces him and orders Lakṣmaṇa to consecrate him as the king of the rākṣasas with ocean water. The leaders debate how to cross the sea. Following Vibhīṣaṇa’s advice, Rāma decides to petition the ocean deity. He spreads a bed of kuśa grass on the shore and lies down, seeking a way forward.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa is consecrated as the future king.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुर्दशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma waits on kuśa grass for three nights, but the ocean remains indifferent. Rejecting forbearance as an ineffective sāman method, he strings his bow and shoots arrows into the depths. These missiles pierce the water like thunderbolts, distressing the nāgas and sea creatures. Churning waves rise while smoke swirls across the surface. Rāma threatens to dry the sea entirely, transforming the horizon into a site of violent upheaval.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma attacks the ocean after being ignored.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चदशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sāgara rises from the deep to meet Rāma. He explains that his waters cannot be solidified but offers to support a bridge built by Nala, the son of the architect Viśvakarman. The vānara army gathers śāla trees, palms, and rocks, throwing them into the waves. This setu stretches one hundred yojanas. Led by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the host crosses to the southern shore.
chapters.subtitle: Nala and the monkeys build the bridge.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षोडशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa sends his ministers Śuka and Sāraṇa to spy on the vānara army. The spies take the form of monkeys, but Vibhīṣaṇa detects and captures them. Rāma releases the pair and invites them to inspect his camp freely. He sends a message challenging Rāvaṇa to face his arrows at dawn. Returning to Laṅkā, the spies describe the formidable strength of Rāma and his allies, urging the king to return Maithilī.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma releases Rāvaṇa's spies.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्तदशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa ascends his palace to overlook the monkey forces. Refusing to return Sītā, he watches as Sāraṇa identifies the commanders. Sāraṇa points out Nīla, the crown prince Aṅgada, and the silver-furred Śveta. These leaders command millions of warriors who prepare for battle. The spies describe the strength and territories of each general, signaling the imminent assault on the walls of Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Sāraṇa identifies the monkey commanders.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टादशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vānara and bear commanders gather their forces to assault Laṅkā. Hara drags a long, multi-colored tail across the earth while leading thousands. The bear king Dhūmra stands near his brother Jāmbavān. Other leaders like Rambha scale mountain peaks as Pramathi stirs up dust clouds. Gavākṣa leads black-faced golaṅgūla monkeys, and Śatabali prepares a force to level the city's defenses.
chapters.subtitle: Scouts describe the leaders of the army.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकोनविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Śuka identifies the leaders of the approaching army to Rāvaṇa. He points out the brothers Mainda and Dvivida. He describes Hanumān, the son of Vāyu who once leaped toward the sun. Beside the archer Rāma stands Lakṣmaṇa. Vibhīṣaṇa stands as the newly consecrated king of the rākṣasas. Sugrīva appears at the center, wearing a golden garland and leading thousands of warriors toward the walls of Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Śuka identifies the enemy leaders.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे विंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa rebukes Śuka and Sāraṇa for praising the enemy and banishes them. He summons new spies to observe Rāma’s military plans. These rākṣasa agents travel to Suvela mountain in disguise. However, Vibhīṣaṇa identifies the intruders. The vānara army captures and beats the spies, who eventually flee back to Laṅkā to report the strength of the approaching forces.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa sends new spies to Rāma’s camp.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: The spy Śārdūla returns to Laṅkā after being captured and paraded by the vānara forces at Suvela mountain. He reports that Rāma has bridged the ocean and stands at the city gates. Refusing to surrender Sītā, Rāvaṇa demands a detailed census of the enemy’s strength. Śārdūla enumerates the monkey generals, including Sugrīva, Hanumān, and Aṅgada. He warns of Rāma’s skill and Vibhīṣaṇa's alliance.
chapters.subtitle: A spy describes Rāma’s army to Rāvaṇa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्वाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Spies report the arrival of Rāma at Mount Suvela. Rāvaṇa commands the sorcerer Vidyujihva to craft an illusory head and bow. Rāvaṇa enters the aśokavanikā and tells a grieving Sītā that his generals slaughtered the sleeping army. The sorcerer casts the fabricated head and a massive bow at her feet. Rāvaṇa declares her husband dead and orders her to submit.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa deceives Sītā with an illusory head.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā gazes at the severed head and golden bow, falling to the earth in grief. She blames Kaikeyī for the ruin of the royal line. Sītā begs Rāvaṇa to slay her. When a messenger summons Rāvaṇa to meet his ministers, the illusory objects vanish. Rāvaṇa departs the aśokavanikā and commands his generals to gather the army for battle by sounding the drums.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā mourns and Rāvaṇa prepares for war.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुर्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Saramā approaches Sītā to reveal that the severed head shown by Rāvaṇa was a deception. She explains that Rāma has crossed the ocean and remains stationed on the southern shore. As the rumble of bherī drums fills the air, Saramā describes the rākṣasa troops preparing for war. She assures Sītā that Rāma will soon destroy his enemies, allowing her to finally unbind her hair in joy.
chapters.subtitle: Saramā reveals the deception to Sītā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Saramā consoles Sītā in the aśokavanikā and spies on Rāvaṇa’s council. She overhears the king’s mother and a senior minister urging him to return Sītā. Rāvaṇa refuses, resolving to die in battle. Saramā returns to the grove to report the king's obstinacy. The sound of vānara drums and conchs shakes the earth, terrifying the rākṣasa guards.
chapters.subtitle: Saramā reports Rāvaṇa's council plans.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षड्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma marches toward Laṅkā as the sound of conches and drums fills the air. Rāvaṇa consults his ministers. The elder Mālyavān advises the king to return Sītā and seek sandhi to preserve the kingdom. He warns that adharma has weakened the rākṣasa army. Dark omens appear: clouds rain hot blood and vultures gather. Mālyavān identifies Rāma as Viṣṇu and urges peace.
chapters.subtitle: Mālyavān advises peace with Rāma.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्तविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa rejects the counsel of Mālyavān and refuses to return Sītā. He insists his svabhāva prevents him from yielding. He organizes the defense of Laṅkā: Prahasta at the eastern gate, Mahāpārśva and Mahodara at the south, and Indrajit at the west. Rāvaṇa guards the northern gate with Śuka and Sāraṇa before withdrawing to his inner chambers.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa organizes the defense of Laṅkā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa reports on the defenses of Laṅkā after his ministers scout the city. He details the placement of Rāvaṇa’s generals and the size of the rākṣasa army. Rāma assigns Nīla to the east, Aṅgada to the south, and Hanumān to the west, while he and Lakṣmaṇa target the north gate. The vānara troops must maintain their animal forms. The army then advances toward Mount Suvela.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma positions the vānara commanders.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकोनत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma ascends Mount Suvela with Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva, and Vibhīṣaṇa. From the summit, they observe the city of Laṅkā and its rākṣasa guards lining the walls. Rāma expresses his intent to punish the enemy for the abduction of Sītā. As the sun sets and the full moon rises, the vānara troops roar toward the city before the army rests upon the mountain peak.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma observes Laṅkā from Mount Suvela.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: The army awakens on Mount Suvela and moves through the groves of campaka and aśoka trees. As the vānaras advance, their feet raise clouds of dust. From the slopes, Rāma and his commanders observe the city on Mount Trikūṭa. They see white towers, golden walls, and a palace with a thousand pillars. The army studies the fortified gates and the vast defenses protecting the stronghold.
chapters.subtitle: The army views the city of Laṅkā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma leads his army to the walls of Laṅkā. He stations vānara generals at every gate, surrounding the city. Acting as an envoy, Aṅgada enters Rāvaṇa’s palace and delivers an ultimatum. When the king orders his seizure, Aṅgada leaps to the roof with four guards, hurls them down, and shatters the building's peak. He returns to Rāma as the siege begins.
chapters.subtitle: Aṅgada delivers Rāma’s ultimatum.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa watches as vānara troops surround Laṅkā, filling moats and smashing gateways. Monkeys station themselves at the gates: Kumuda at the east, Śatabali at the south, Suṣeṇa at the west, and Rāma at the north with Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa. At the king’s command, the rākṣasa army rushes out. A battle erupts where warriors use tridents and swords against trees and stones.
chapters.subtitle: The siege begins and both sides clash.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रयस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vānara and rākṣasa warriors clash in individual combat. Aṅgada smashes the chariot of Indrajit, while Hanumān crushes Jambumālī. Rāma decapitates four rākṣasa commanders with arrows. Using uprooted aśvakarṇa and saptaparṇa trees, vānara leaders strike down their foes. Nīla beheads Nikumbha with a chariot wheel. Fallen elephants and broken axles litter the earth as the rākṣasas continue fighting.
chapters.subtitle: Warriors fight individual duels.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Night falls, and the armies clash in the dark. Vānaras tear at chariot horses with their teeth. Rāma’s arrows light the sky as the Trikūṭa mountain echoes the roar. After Aṅgada destroys his chariot, Indrajit vanishes using magic. From the air, he launches arrows that transform into venomous serpents, binding Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
chapters.subtitle: Indrajit uses serpent arrows during a night battle.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चत्रिंशः सर्गः
