chapters.es: Rāma commands ten vānara leaders to locate the invisible Indrajit. Concealed by darkness, Rāvaṇa’s son discharges serpent-like arrows that pierce the brothers’ vital points. Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa fall to the earth, their bodies covered by shafts. Bound by the śarabandha, they lie motionless. Hanumān and the monkey host gather around the fallen princes while the enemy boasts of victory.
chapters.subtitle: Indrajit binds the princes.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa lie motionless on a bed of arrows. While the monkey leaders weep, Vibhīṣaṇa uses a boon to spot the invisible Indrajit. Indrajit declares the princes defeated and returns to Laṅkā. Sugrīva despairs, but Vibhīṣaṇa encourages him to maintain the army's morale. Within the city walls, Rāvaṇa embraces his son, rejoicing in the news that his enemies have fallen.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa rallies the army.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa orders the rākṣasī guards to take Sītā to the battlefield in the puṣpaka aerial car. He intends for her to see the fallen princes and lose hope. From the air, Sītā observes the motionless vānara army. She finds Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa lying on the earth, their bodies pierced by arrows and their bows cast aside. Believing them dead, she laments.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā views the fallen princes from the air.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā mourns her apparent widowhood, questioning the predictions of astrologers. The rākṣasī Trijaṭā comforts her, pointing out that the puṣpaka chariot remains stable and the brothers’ faces retain their lakṣmī, or vital glow. Trijaṭā insists that the army’s composure proves they survive. Sītā returns to the aśokavanikā, balancing these hopeful signs against her immediate distress.
chapters.subtitle: Trijaṭā reassures Sītā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma regains consciousness and beholds Lakṣmaṇa lying motionless. Overcome by grief, he declares that victory and Sītā do not matter without his brother. Rāma urges Sugrīva and the vānara army to abandon the siege and return across the ocean, attributing the defeat to daiva. As the monkeys weep, Vibhīṣaṇa approaches with a mace, causing the ranks to flee in temporary confusion.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma regains consciousness and grieves.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sugrīva rallies the vānara troops as Vibhīṣaṇa mourns the princes. A sudden wind sweeps the battlefield as the divine bird Garuḍa descends. The serpents binding Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa flee at his sight. Garuḍa heals their wounds with a touch, restoring their vigor. He identifies himself as their friend before soaring into the sky. Revitalized, the army marches toward the gates of Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Garuḍa heals Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa learns that Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa have escaped the śarabandha. Disturbed by their recovery, he commands Dhūmrākṣa to lead a massive host toward the west gate. As the general departs, a vulture settles on his chariot and blood rains from the sky. Despite these omens, Dhūmrākṣa marches forward to confront the soldiers protected by the Rāghava brothers.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa sends Dhūmrākṣa to attack.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vānara warriors and rākṣasas clash using uprooted trees and iron tridents. The leader Dhūmrākṣa scatters the monkey ranks with his bow. Hanumān intervenes, first smashing Dhūmrākṣa’s chariot with a boulder. Though struck on the head by a spiked mace, Hanumān drops a mountain peak onto Dhūmrākṣa, crushing his limbs. The surviving rākṣasas flee to Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān kills Dhūmrākṣa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Akampana advances on a golden chariot. As the rākṣasa and vānara armies collide, they stir a thick dust cloud. Blinded by the haze, warriors accidentally kill their own comrades. The dust settles as blood soaks the ground. Amidst the carnage, the leaders Kumuda, Nala, and Mainda use uprooted trees and mountain peaks to crush the enemy ranks.
chapters.subtitle: Akampana leads his army into battle.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Akampana drives his chariot into the battle, scattering the vānaras. Hanumān intervenes, weathering a shower of arrows to uproot a mountain peak. When arrows shatter the stone, Hanumān seizes an aśvakarṇa tree. He whirls the trunk to crush chariots and soldiers before striking Akampana’s head with another tree. The rākṣasa falls dead, and his army flees toward Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān kills Akampana.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa inspects the defenses of Laṅkā and commands Prahastha to lead the rākṣasa host. Prahastha mobilizes the army, which departs through the eastern gate. Dark omens emerge as vultures circle the general’s chariot and blood rains from the sky. The vānara army meets the charge with boulders and uprooted trees. Prahastha plunges into the conflict.
chapters.subtitle: Prahastha leads the rākṣasa host.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Prahastha leads the rākṣasa army into a clash where vānara warriors fight with stones. After the monkey leaders kill Prahastha's lieutenants, Nīla confronts the general. Prahastha abandons his broken chariot to fight with a heavy mallet. He strikes Nīla’s forehead, but the monkey commander responds by crushing Prahastha’s skull with a massive rock. The remaining rākṣasas retreat to Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Nīla kills Prahastha in direct combat.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa enters the battlefield in a golden chariot. Vibhīṣaṇa identifies the rākṣasa leaders as Rāvaṇa strikes Sugrīva and Nīla. Hanumān trades blows with the king and carries the wounded Lakṣmaṇa to safety after a śakti strike. Rāma, mounted on Hanumān’s back, destroys Rāvaṇa’s horses and shatters his crown with an ardhacandra arrow. Rāma declines to kill the weaponless king, permitting him to retreat.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma defeats Rāvaṇa and allows his retreat.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa orders the awakening of Kumbhakarṇa, who lies in a cursed slumber. Servants enter his cave, piling heaps of meat and jars of blood. They beat drums, blow conches, and drive elephants over his limbs. Upon waking, the rākṣasa devours the feast and drinks pots of wine. He strides through the city to meet his brother, his form scattering the panicked vānara troops.
chapters.subtitle: Demons awaken the sleeping Kumbhakarṇa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma questions Vibhīṣaṇa about the mountain-like Kumbhakarṇa. Vibhīṣaṇa recounts how the son of Viśravas once defeated Indra. To save the universe, Brahmā cursed him to a sleep resembling death, waking for only one day every six months. Rāvaṇa has now roused him. Rāma orders Nīla to position the vānara army at the gates and bridges of Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa recounts the history of Kumbhakarṇa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Kumbhakarṇa marches to the golden palace, where he finds Rāvaṇa in distress. Rāvaṇa explains that Rāma and the vānara host have crossed the ocean and killed the chief rākṣasa commanders. With resources exhausted, the king begs his brother to save the inhabitants. He urges Kumbhakarṇa to scatter the enemy forces like a powerful wind dispersing clouds.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa asks Kumbhakarṇa for help.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Kumbhakarṇa reminds Rāvaṇa that his suffering stems from ignoring wise counsel. He explains a ruler’s duty to balance dharma, artha, and kāma. When Rāvaṇa bristles, Kumbhakarṇa quickly consoles him. He vows to march onto the battlefield and destroy the vānara army. He promises to slay Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa with his bare hands and bring their heads to Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Kumbhakarṇa promises to destroy the enemy.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्विपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Mahodara dismisses Kumbhakarṇa’s plan to confront Rāma alone, recalling the slaughter at Janasthāna. He proposes a ruse where rākṣasas return from the field carrying arrows marked with Rāma’s name to feign his death. Once rumors spread, Rāvaṇa should approach a grieving Sītā. Mahodara argues that this deception will force her submission without further risking the army in direct combat.
chapters.subtitle: Mahodara proposes a ruse to win Sītā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Kumbhakarṇa armors himself for battle. Rāvaṇa adorns his brother with jewels and hands him a flaming iron śūla. Ignoring ill omens of falling meteors, the giant increases his size and leaps over the city walls. His loud roar scatters the vānara troops, who fall like uprooted trees. Wielding his pike, he advances toward the enemy like the personification of time.
chapters.subtitle: Kumbhakarṇa armors himself and roars.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Kumbhakarṇa roars across the battlefield, scattering the vānara army. Fleeing monkeys hide in caves or leap into the sea. Aṅgada halts the retreat, rebuking the warriors and invoking the reward of Brahmaloka for those who fall in combat. Rallied by these words, Hanumān and the other chiefs turn back to face the advancing rākṣasa once more.
chapters.subtitle: Aṅgada rallies the retreating army.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: After crushing the vānara army and capturing Sugrīva, the giant Kumbhakarṇa resumes his rampage. Sugrīva escapes by biting the giant's nose and ears. Rāma intervenes, striking the rākṣasa with arrows before using the vāyavyāstra to sever his arms. After lopping off his legs, Rāma decapitates Kumbhakarṇa with the aindrāstra. The torso sinks into the ocean, ending the giant's threat.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma kills Kumbhakarṇa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa collapses upon learning that Rāma has slain Kumbhakarṇa. The king laments the loss of his right arm, the warrior who once paralyzed the devas. He anticipates the vānara army scaling the walls of Laṅkā. Despairing over Sītā and his kingdom, Rāvaṇa regrets rejecting the counsel of Vibhīṣaṇa. He acknowledges this defeat as the fruit of his own actions.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa mourns his brother.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa sends his sons and brothers into the fray. Triśiras, Atikāya, Devāntaka, and Narāntaka enter the battlefield with a massive rākṣasa host. The vānara army meets them with boulders. Narāntaka rides a swift horse, piercing hundreds with his lance. Aṅgada intercepts him, shattering the rider's spear against his chest. With a single palm strike, Aṅgada kills the horse and crushes Narāntaka.
chapters.subtitle: Aṅgada kills Narāntaka.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Following the fall of Narāntaka, the rākṣasa leaders Mahodara, Devāntaka, and Triśira converge on Aṅgada. Hanumān joins the fray, shattering Devāntaka’s skull with a single fist, while Nīla crushes Mahodara beneath a mountain peak. Hanumān then seizes Triśira’s sword and severs his three heads. Finally, Ṛṣabha kills Mahāpārśva with the demon's own mace.
chapters.subtitle: The monkey army kills four commanders.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Atikāya enters the field in a chariot drawn by a thousand horses, his frame scattering the vānara host. Vibhīṣaṇa identifies him as the son of Rāvaṇa, protected by divine armor. Lakṣmaṇa intercepts the warrior, exchanging celestial missiles. When ordinary shafts fail to pierce the rākṣasa’s mail, Lakṣmaṇa invokes the brahmāstra, which severs the warrior’s crowned head, sending it crashing to the earth.
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa kills Atikāya.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: After the fall of his kinsmen, Indrajit performs a fire sacrifice at Nikumbhila. He invokes the brahmāstra and vanishes into the sky. Hidden by clouds, he rains arrows upon the vānara host, wounding the leaders. Recognizing the power of the creator’s weapon, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa endure the strikes until they fall unconscious. Believing them defeated, Indrajit returns to Laṅkā to announce his success to Rāvaṇa.
chapters.subtitle: Indrajit wounds Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa and Hanumān find thousands of monkeys fallen to the brahmāstra. The aged Jāmbavān directs Hanumān to fetch four healing herbs from the Himālaya mountains: mṛtasañjīvanī, viśalyakaraṇī, suvarṇakaraṇī, and sandhānī. Hanumān uproots the entire mountain peak. He carries the glowing mass to Laṅkā, where the scent of the plants heals Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and the army.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān fetches medicinal herbs.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sugrīva orders vānara troops to invade Laṅkā with torches. Monkeys set fire to mansions and gates. The city glows like a forest of kiṃśuka blossoms. Rāma draws his bow, shattering a gate with one shaft. The twang of his bowstring, the jyā, echoes above the noise. In response, Rāvaṇa sends Kumbha and Nikumbha with a fresh army to meet the monkeys in combat.
chapters.subtitle: The monkeys set fire to Laṅkā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Aṅgada crushes Kampana before facing Kumbha, the son of Kumbhakarṇa. Kumbha pierces the vānara leaders Dvivida and Mainda with arrows and nearly overcomes Aṅgada. Sugrīva rushes to the front, breaks Kumbha’s bow, and engages the rākṣasa in hand-to-hand combat. After enduring heavy strikes, Sugrīva delivers a blow to Kumbha’s chest with his closed fist. The warrior falls dead to the earth.
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva kills Kumbha.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुःषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Nikumbha seizes a heavy parigha adorned with diamonds. He whirls the iron club and strikes Hanumān on the chest. The weapon shatters into fragments. Hanumān retaliates with a fist blow. Although Nikumbha briefly lifts him, Hanumān frees himself, pins the demon to the ground, and rips off his head. The surrounding armies of the rākṣasas and vānaras then resume their struggle.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān kills Nikumbha.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Following the deaths of Kumbha and Nikumbha, Rāvaṇa orders Makarākṣa, the son of Khara, to the battlefield. The warrior mounts his chariot, vowing to slay Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. As the rākṣasa host marches to the sound of conchs and drums, several dark omens appear: the driver’s whip falls and horses weep. Ignoring these signs, the soldiers advance toward the enemy lines.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa sends Makarākṣa to battle.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Makarākṣa leads his army into battle. After the demon scatters the vānara ranks, Rāma intervenes. Makarākṣa challenges Rāma to avenge his father, Khara. Rāma shatters the demon’s bow and chariot before destroying a flaming śūla. Finally, Rāma looses the pāvakāstra, piercing Makarākṣa’s heart. The remaining night-rangers flee toward Laṅkā as their leader falls like a mountain struck by lightning.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma kills Makarākṣa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Indrajit performs a ritual using vibhītaka fuel. After securing the favor of Agni, he ascends a golden chariot and vanishes. Hidden by smoke, he rains steel arrows upon the brothers, leaving them bloodied like kiṃśuka trees. When Lakṣmaṇa proposes using the brahmāstra, Rāma restrains him, refusing to kill those not engaged in direct combat.
chapters.subtitle: Indrajit fights invisibly with steel arrows.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Indrajit emerges from Laṅkā, placing an illusory māyā-sītā in his chariot. Hanumān and the vānara army charge, only to halt in horror. Indrajit seizes the figure by her hair and strikes her with a sword. He declares he is destroying the motive for their war. The blade cuts her, and she falls to the earth. Indrajit roars, leaving the monkeys in despair.
chapters.subtitle: Indrajit kills an illusory Sītā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकोनसप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān rallies the vānara troops to reclaim their valor. The monkeys charge while Indrajit counters with a barrage of arrows. Hanumān hurls a rock at the prince’s chariot, but the driver maneuvers away. To report the apparent death of Sītā, Hanumān orders a retreat toward Rāma. Seeing the enemy depart, Indrajit proceeds to Nikumbhilā to perform a blood sacrifice.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān retreats to report Sītā's death.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma sends Jāmbavān to aid Hanumān. Hanumān returns with news that Indrajit killed Sītā. Distraught, Rāma falls to the earth. Lakṣmaṇa delivers a critique of dharma, arguing that righteousness is useless if the virtuous suffer. Contending that power and artha are the true roots of success, he urges his brother to rise and destroy their enemies.
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa critiques dharma after the news.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकसप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa finds Rāma collapsed in grief. Upon hearing of Sītā’s death, he dismisses the report as māyā intended to demoralize the army. He explains that Indrajit has retreated to Nikumbhilā to perform a homa that would grant him invincibility. Vibhīṣaṇa urges Rāma to dispatch Lakṣmaṇa to disrupt the ritual, as killing the prince is only possible before the sacrifice concludes.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa explains the illusory Sītā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्विसप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma sets aside his grief and directs Lakṣmaṇa to slay the son of Rāvaṇa. Arming himself with a golden bow, Lakṣmaṇa touches Rāma’s feet and vows to strike the enemy. He marches alongside Hanumān and Vibhīṣaṇa toward the ritual grove. Upon reaching the site, Lakṣmaṇa observes the rākṣasa forces standing in battle formation and readies his bow.
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa sets out to stop Indrajit.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रिसप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa urges Lakṣmaṇa to attack before Indrajit finishes his ritual. The vānara army clashes with the rākṣasas. Hearing his army's cries, Indrajit leaves his sacrifice and mounts his chariot. Hanumān crushes thousands with massive trees. Vibhīṣaṇa points out Indrajit to Lakṣmaṇa, directing the prince to fire his arrows and end the life of Rāvaṇa’s son.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān and Lakṣmaṇa attack the grove.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुःसप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa leads Lakṣmaṇa to a dark nyagrodha tree where Indrajit performs rituals. Lakṣmaṇa stands ready, challenging the prince. Arriving in a chariot, Indrajit insults his uncle for betraying their lineage. Vibhīṣaṇa responds by detailing the sins of Rāvaṇa, including the theft of wives and the slaughter of sages. He renounces his kin for their adharma, leaving Indrajit to face Lakṣmaṇa.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa and Indrajit exchange insults.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चसप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Indrajit advances, threatening to send his enemies to the abode of Yama. Lakṣmaṇa mocks his previous use of invisibility as the tactic of a thief. Indrajit releases arrows like hissing serpents, covering Lakṣmaṇa in blood. Lakṣmaṇa retaliates, striking the rākṣasa’s chest with five shafts. The two archers continue their duel, discharging volleys like rain clouds.
chapters.subtitle: The duel of Indrajit and Lakṣmaṇa begins.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षट्सप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa draws his bow against Indrajit after Vibhīṣaṇa identifies signs of the demon’s waning confidence. Indrajit launches a barrage of shafts. Lakṣmaṇa shatters Indrajit’s golden armor. The archers trade a dense rain of arrows that fills the sky. Bathed in blood, the combatants resemble flowering kiṃśuka trees. Neither warrior shows fatigue as Vibhīṣaṇa moves to support the prince.
chapters.subtitle: The archers trade a rain of arrows.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्तसप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa looses arrows upon the rākṣasa ranks while urging the vānara leaders to strike. Hanumān and Jāmbavān crush the enemy with trees. In a duel of swift archery, Lakṣmaṇa and Indrajit veil the sky with shafts. Lakṣmaṇa slays Indrajit’s four horses and beheads his charioteer. Four monkey chiefs leap upon the chariot to trample the steeds, forcing Indrajit to fight on foot.
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa destroys Indrajit's chariot.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टसप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: After losing his horses, Indrajit fights on foot, exchanging volleys with Lakṣmaṇa. Vibhīṣaṇa joins the fray, piercing his nephew’s chest. Invoking the righteousness of Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa draws the aindrāstra. This final arrow severs Indrajit’s head, which falls to the earth still adorned with golden earrings. The rākṣasa army scatters in panic as the vānara host celebrates.
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa decapitates Indrajit with the aindrāstra.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकोनाशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa returns to Rāma to report the death of Indrajit. Vibhīṣaṇa confirms the kill, and Rāma embraces his brother. Rāma instructs the physician Suṣeṇa to treat the injured. Suṣeṇa administers a medicinal scent that removes arrows and closes Lakṣmaṇa’s wounds. Once restored, Lakṣmaṇa stands healthy. The physician also treats Vibhīṣaṇa and the vānara warriors.
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa is healed by Suṣeṇa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Ministers report the death of Indrajit, sending Rāvaṇa into grief. His sorrow turns to rage. Drawing a sword, he rushes toward the aśokavanikā to kill Sītā. Sītā trembles and laments. The minister Supārśva stays Rāvaṇa’s hand, advising him that killing a woman violates dharma. Rāvaṇa relents and returns to his assembly to prepare for a final confrontation.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa attempts to kill Sītā in rage.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकाशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa sends his forces to surround Rāma. While vānaras fight with teeth and nails, the rākṣasas deploy maces. Seeking protection, the monkeys turn to Rāma, who invokes a gāndharva weapon. He moves with such speed that the enemy sees thousands of his form. Bewildered, the rākṣasas slay each other. Rāma destroys the army in an afternoon, leaving the field like the ground where Rudra sports.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma destroys the army with a gāndharva weapon.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्व्यशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rākṣasa women gather in Laṅkā to lament their fallen kinsmen. They trace the city’s ruin to Śūrpaṇakhā’s encounter with Rāma and Rāvaṇa’s refusal to return Sītā. The widows recall Rāma slaying Khara and Vālin. They mourn Rāvaṇa’s rejection of Vibhīṣaṇa’s counsel, which transformed the city into a śmaśāna. The grieving families wail as their end approaches.
chapters.subtitle: The widows of Laṅkā lament.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्र्यशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa erupts in fury and commands Mahodara, Mahāpārśva, and Virūpākṣa to mobilize the remaining army. Ascending a chariot, he vows to avenge fallen kin by slaughtering the vānara host. Despite grim portents—a darkened sun and raining blood—he charges into the fray. Gold-plumed shafts fly from his bow, piercing the hearts of the monkey warriors.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa leads his final host to battle.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुरशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa scatters the vānara army with a hail of arrows. Sugrīva rallies his troops and charges Virūpākṣa, who enters on an elephant. When Sugrīva strikes the beast, the rākṣasa leaps down with sword and shield. They exchange strikes until Sugrīva hits his opponent's temple with a palm-blow. Virūpākṣa falls dead, as the surrounding armies roar.
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva kills Virūpākṣa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चाशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa commands Mahodara to attack. Mahodara charges and encounters Sugrīva. The two trade blows using rocks and sāla trees. When Mahodara’s horses fall to Sugrīva’s parigha, the combatants fight with a gadā and then bare fists. They eventually seize swords. Seizing an opening, Sugrīva swings his sword and severs Mahodara’s head. Rāma and the monkeys celebrate the victory.
chapters.subtitle: Sugrīva kills Mahodara.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षडशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Mahāpārśva decapitates vānara warriors before Jāmbavān crushes his chariot. Aṅgada hurls a radiant iron parigha at the demon’s head and slaps his cheek. Mahāpārśva retaliates, swinging an oiled paraśvadha. Dodging the axe, Aṅgada clenches a fist and strikes the demon’s chest. This blow shatters Mahāpārśva’s heart. The rākṣasa army falls into panic while Rāvaṇa watches in fury.
chapters.subtitle: Aṅgada kills Mahāpārśva.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्ताशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa drives a thundering chariot toward the monkey army. After scattering the monkeys with a tāmasa weapon, he encounters the two brothers like Rāhu approaching the sun and moon. Rāvaṇa intercepts Lakṣmaṇa's shafts and duels Rāma directly. Their arrows darken the sky. Rāvaṇa strikes Rāma’s forehead, but Rāma retaliates with missiles. Rāma dissolves Rāvaṇa's serpent-arrows using pāvaka weapons.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma and Rāvaṇa trade celestial missiles.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टाशीतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa hurls discuses, which Rāma meets with gāndharva weapons. When Lakṣmaṇa shatters Rāvaṇa’s bow and Vibhīṣaṇa kills his horses, the rākṣasa hurls a magical śakti spear. The weapon pierces Lakṣmaṇa’s chest, pinning him to the earth. Rāma wrenches the spear from his brother’s body while enduring a shower of arrows. He then initiates a final exchange of shafts.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa injures Lakṣmaṇa with a śakti spear.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकोननवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma laments over the fallen Lakṣmaṇa. The physician Suṣeṇa identifies signs of life and sends Hanumān to fetch medicinal herbs. Unable to recognize the plants, Hanumān uproots the entire peak and carries it through the sky. Suṣeṇa administers the crushed viśalyakaraṇī herb through Lakṣmaṇa’s nostrils. Revived, Lakṣmaṇa stands and urges Rāma to slay Rāvaṇa.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān fetches the mountain again.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे नवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma stands on the earth to face the chariot-borne Rāvaṇa until Indra sends his own vehicle driven by Mātali. Equipped with Indra’s bow and armor, Rāma ascends the car. Rāvaṇa unleashes fire-breathing serpents, but Rāma counters with the gārutmata missile, transforming his shafts into eagles. When Rāvaṇa strikes the horses, planets like Budha and Aṅgāraka threaten the stars.
chapters.subtitle: Indra sends a chariot to Rāma.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकनवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma’s fury causes the earth to tremble. Rāvaṇa hurls a massive trident that incinerates Rāma’s arrows. In response, Rāma wields a golden śakti provided by Mātali, which shatters the trident mid-air. Rāma then strikes Rāvaṇa with sharp arrows, piercing his forehead and chest. Covered in blood, the demon king resembles a blossoming aśoka tree as the carnage intensifies.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma shatters Rāvaṇa’s trident.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्विनवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa rains arrows upon Rāma, who stands immovable. Covered in blood, Rāma resembles a kiṃśuka tree. He rebukes Rāvaṇa for the abduction of Sītā, dismissing his heroism as the act of a thief. As Rāma’s strength increases, he overwhelms the king with a relentless volley. Facing death and unable to return fire, a bewildered Rāvaṇa falters, prompting his charioteer to withdraw.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma rebukes Rāvaṇa and overwhelms him.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रिनवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa rebukes his sārathi for withdrawing, accusing him of cowardice. The charioteer defends his loyalty, explaining that the rathavājinaḥ were exhausted and that a driver must judge the warrior’s fatigue. Pleased by this reasoning, Rāvaṇa rewards him with a golden ornament. Vindicated, the driver turns the horses back toward Rāma, positioning the chariot for the final fray.
chapters.subtitle: The charioteer defends his decision.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुर्नवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma watches Rāvaṇa’s chariot approach and directs Mātali to drive Indra’s chariot forward. As the warriors clash, gandharvas gather in the sky. Dark omens haunt Rāvaṇa: vultures follow his wheels and his horses weep. Laṅkā turns a deep red as if the earth were burning. Encouraged by auspicious signs and his skill, Rāma increases his speed to meet the rākṣasa king.
chapters.subtitle: The final chariot duel begins.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चनवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma and Rāvaṇa engage in a duel that brings both armies to a standstill. Rāvaṇa targets the flag of Indra’s chariot, but Rāma fells the banner with an arrow. Rāvaṇa showers the divine horses with weapons, yet they remain steady as if struck by padmanāla stems. Thousands of arrows from both sides saturate the air, leaving no breathing space in the sky.
chapters.subtitle: The armies watch the final duel.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षण्णवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma and Rāvaṇa release arrow showers that churn the seas and disturb the dānavas. Rāma severs Rāvaṇa’s head with a kṣura arrow, but a matching head immediately rises in its place. Although a hundred heads fall to Rāma’s shafts, the rākṣasa king remains alive. Troubled that his weapons fail, Rāma maintains his attack as the battle persists through the night.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa’s heads regrow as they are severed.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्तनवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Mātali urges Rāma to deploy the brahmāstra. Rāma fits the arrow gifted by Agastya to his bow. The missile pierces Rāvaṇa’s chest and enters the earth before returning to the quiver. As the king of rākṣasas falls like Vṛtra, his army flees. Vānaras shout in victory while flowers fall from the sky. Vibhīṣaṇa and Sugrīva gather to honor the victor.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma kills Rāvaṇa with the brahmāstra.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टनवतितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Following the death of Rāvaṇa, the women of the inner chambers rush to the battlefield. They fall upon his body, clutching his limbs and bathing his face in tears. The widows lament that a warrior who once terrified the gods fell to a mortal. They recall how he ignored the counsel of Vibhīṣaṇa, attributing the destruction of the rākṣasa race to daiva.
chapters.subtitle: The women of Laṅkā mourn Rāvaṇa.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकोनशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Mandodarī gazes upon the body of Rāvaṇa, mourning his fatal obsession with Sītā. Vibhīṣaṇa initially refuses to perform the funeral rites, but Rāma insists that hostilities must end at death. Accepting this, Vibhīṣaṇa offers the sacred fire for the saṃskāra. After the widows depart, Rāma celebrates with his army, much like Indra after defeating Vṛtra.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa performs the funeral rites.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे शततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma dismisses Mātali and Indra’s chariot. After embracing Sugrīva, Rāma orders the formal consecration of Vibhīṣaṇa. Lakṣmaṇa pours water from a golden ghaṭa to install him as the king of Laṅkā. The new ruler accepts offerings and presents them to the brothers. Finally, Rāma sends Hanumān into the city to inform Sītā of the victory.
chapters.subtitle: Vibhīṣaṇa is consecrated as King of Laṅkā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān enters Laṅkā to bring Sītā news of Rāma’s victory. He recounts the death of Rāvaṇa and the installation of Vibhīṣaṇa. When Hanumān offers to punish the rākṣasī guards, Sītā restrains him. She insists that a noble person must show mercy to all, as no one is without fault. Expressing her longing, she asks to see her husband.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān brings news of victory to Sītā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्व्यधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Hanumān informs Rāma of Sītā’s desire. Rāma instructs Vibhīṣaṇa to bring her adorned in jewelry. When guards disperse the crowd, Rāma intervenes, asserting that a woman’s character serves as her true protection. He insists she walk through the assembly. Sītā, shrinking with modesty and weeping, approaches her husband to gaze upon his face before the gathered army.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā appears before the army.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्र्यधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma addresses Maithilī, declaring that his victory restores his family's honor. He tells Sītā that his military efforts served to wipe away insult rather than reclaim her. He compares her to a lamp painful to sore eyes and orders her to leave, suggesting she seek shelter with Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, or Sugrīva. Sītā stands weeping, trembling like a vine struck by an elephant.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma publicly rejects Sītā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुरधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Distressed by the rejection, Sītā defends her character, stating her heart remained devoted while captive. She requests Lakṣmaṇa to prepare a funeral pyre. After circumambulating Rāma and invoking the fire god Pāvaka as a witness to her purity, she steps into the flames. A crowd of monkeys and demons watches as she offers herself to the fire to prove her innocence.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā enters the fire pyre.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: The guardians of the world descend in vimāna chariots. While Sītā stands near the fire, they ask why the creator acts as a common man. Rāma declares himself the human son of Daśaratha. In response, Brahmā identifies him as Nārāyaṇa and the four-armed Viṣṇu carrying the śārṅga bow. Sītā is revealed as Lakṣmī. Brahmā explains Rāma assumed human form specifically to slay Rāvaṇa.
chapters.subtitle: Brahmā identifies Rāma as Viṣṇu.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षडधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhāvasu emerges from the flames carrying Vaidehī. She appears sinless in thought, word, and sight. The fire god declares her purity despite her captivity in Rāvaṇa’s palace. Rāma explains that he permitted her ordeal only to satisfy the public and establish her purity across the three worlds. Rāma accepts his wife, and the couple reunites amidst the praise of the gods.
chapters.subtitle: The fire god returns Sītā to Rāma.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे सप्ताधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Maheśvara reveals King Daśaratha seated within a celestial vimāna. Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa offer salutations to their father. Daśaratha declares his relief at the conclusion of the exile and the destruction of Rāvaṇa. At Rāma’s request, the king rescinds his disowning of Kaikeyī and Bharata. He assures Sītā that her trial proved her purity before returning to the world of Indra.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma meets the celestial Daśaratha.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे अष्टाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Mahendra offers Rāma a boon. Rāma requests that the fallen vānara warriors be restored to life and healed. He also asks that their forests yield fruit in all seasons. Indra grants the wish, and the dead soldiers rise as if from sleep. The gods urge Rāma to return to Ayodhyā to reunite with Bharata and Sītā before they depart for heaven.
chapters.subtitle: Indra revives the fallen monkeys.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे नवाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa offers Rāma luxuries, but Rāma declines, mindful of Bharata’s ascetic life in Ayodhyā. He asks for a swift path home, prompting Vibhīṣaṇa to present the puṣpaka vimāna. This aerial car, crafted by Viśvakarman and seized from Kubera, shines with gold. Rāma urges his friend to prepare the vehicle so he may reunite with his family.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma prepares to return in the puṣpaka.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे दशाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vibhīṣaṇa presents the puṣpaka to Rāma. Before departing, Rāma instructs the king to honor the monkey host with gems. After the distribution, Rāma ascends the aerial car with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa. He grants the vanaras and Vibhīṣaṇa permission to accompany him to Ayodhyā. The assembly boards the vehicle, which rises into the sky as Rāma begins his journey home.
chapters.subtitle: The host boards the aerial chariot.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे एकादशाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma and Sītā board the puṣpaka vimāna. From the air, Rāma points out Trikūṭa and the battlefield. They fly over the nala-setu bridge and the golden Maināka mountain. Rāma identifies the woods of Kiṣkindhā, the Pampā, and the hermitages of Agastya and Atri. After passing the Yamunā and Gaṅgā, the towers of Ayodhyā appear. The vānara army and Vibhīṣaṇa gaze at the capital.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma identifies landmarks from the air.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे द्वादशाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa reach the hermitage of Bharadvāja as their exile concludes. Rāma asks after the welfare of Ayodhyā. The sage confirms that Bharata lives as an ascetic, guarding the royal pāduka. Through his tapas, Bharadvāja recounts the victory over Rāvaṇa and offers a boon. Rāma asks that trees along his path bear fruit out of season, and the road blooms for three yojanas.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma visits the hermitage of Bharadvāja.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे त्रयोदशाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma dispatches Hanumān to Ayodhyā to announce his victory. Hanumān reaches Nandigrāma, finding Bharata clad in bark with matted hair, governing through the pādukā. When Hanumān reveals that Rāma has defeated Rāvaṇa and is returning with Sītā, Bharata collapses from joy. He recovers to embrace the messenger, offering a bounty of cows and villages in gratitude for the news.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān announces Rāma’s return to Bharata.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे चतुर्दशाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Seated on kuśa grass, Hanumān recounts the years of exile. He details the encounter with Virādha, the slaughter at Janasthāna, and the abduction of Sītā by Rāvaṇa. Hanumān explains the alliance with Sugrīva, the killing of Vālin, and the leap across the ocean. He describes the construction of the setu and the fall of the rākṣasa army. Hanumān announces Rāma has reached the Gaṅgā.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān recounts the exile to Bharata.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे पञ्चदशाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Bharata instructs Śatrughna to prepare Ayodhyā. The queens and citizens travel to Nandigrāma, where the puṣpaka vimāna descends. Rāma alights and embraces Bharata, who returns the pādukā to his feet. Bharata formally surrenders the kingdom. After greeting his mothers and the priests, Rāma dismisses the aerial car to return to the god Vaiśravaṇa.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma returns to Ayodhyā.

chapters.name: युद्धकाण्डे षोडशाधिकशततमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Bharata returns the kingdom to Rāma, who accepts the rule. After ceremonial bathing, Rāma enters Ayodhyā. Vasiṣṭha and the sages consecrate him with waters from the four oceans. Rāma distributes gems to his allies, while Sītā grants her pearl necklace to Hanumān. Bharata is appointed to the yauvarājya. During Rāma’s reign, trees bear fruit year-round and disease vanishes from the land.
chapters.subtitle: The coronation of King Rāma.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे प्रथमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sages from the four cardinal directions arrive at Rāma’s palace following his victory over the rākṣasa host. Rāma welcomes Agastya, Vasiṣṭha, and the others with arghya offerings and golden seats. The sages congratulate him on the fall of Rāvaṇa and Kumbhakarṇa but express particular wonder at the death of Indrajit. Rāma asks why this warrior’s defeat deserves more praise than the king’s and requests the history of Indrajit’s power and his victory over Indra.
chapters.subtitle: Sages congratulate Rāma on his victory.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः
chapters.es: The sage Pulastya settles near Mount Meru to perform austerities. When local girls disturb his meditation, he decrees that any woman who looks upon him will conceive. The daughter of King Tṛṇabindu enters the hermitage while the sage recites the Veda and immediately becomes pregnant. Her father offers her to Pulastya in marriage to serve him. Pleased by her devotion, the sage grants her a son named Viśravas, who inherits his father’s practice of penance and Vedic study.
chapters.subtitle: The birth of Viśravas and his ascetic life.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे तृतीयः सर्गः
chapters.es: Viśravas marries the daughter of Bharadvāja and fathers Vaiśravaṇa. The son performs penance, surviving on air and water for thousands of years. Brahmā grants him the status of a lokapāla and the lord of wealth, presenting him with the puṣpaka vimāna. Following his father's counsel, Vaiśravaṇa moves to the abandoned city of Laṅkā, once built by Viśvakarman and vacated by rākṣasas. He settles on the mountain peak, ruling the island city while visiting his parents in his vehicle.
chapters.subtitle: Vaiśravaṇa receives boons and settles in Laṅkā.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma questions Agastya regarding the origins of the first inhabitants of Laṅkā. Agastya describes how Prajāpati created water and appointed guardians; those who vowed to protect it became rākṣasas. From the lineage of Heti, the infant Sukeśa is born and abandoned on Mount Mandara. Śiva and Pārvatī discover the crying child, granting him immortality and an aerial city. Pārvatī further ordains that all rākṣasa offspring shall attain their mother’s age immediately upon birth, allowing Sukeśa to roam the worlds.
chapters.subtitle: Agastya explains the origin of the rākṣasas.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sukeśa and Devavatī produce three sons: Mālyavān, Sumālī, and Mālī. After performing rigid penances on Mount Meru, the brothers receive boons of invincibility and long life from Brahmā. At their request, the architect Viśvakarman directs them to the island city of Laṅkā on Mount Trikūṭa. They marry the daughters of the gandharvī Narmadā and father many rākṣasa warriors. Emboldened by their power, they begin to disrupt sacred sacrifices and harass the gods and sages.
chapters.subtitle: Three rākṣasa brothers receive boons and settle in Laṅkā.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः
chapters.es: The deities and sages seek refuge with Maheśvara to escape the sons of Sukeśa. Because of a prior boon, Maheśvara directs the petitioners to Nārāyaṇa, who pledges to slay the rākṣasa brothers. Learning of this pact, Mālyavān, Māli, and Sumāli march their army out of Laṅkā on chariots and beasts. Despite omens of raining blood and shaking mountains, the host attacks. Viṣṇu mounts Garuḍa and enters the fray, where the rākṣasas surround him with weapons.
chapters.subtitle: The gods seek Viṣṇu's help against the rākṣasas.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Nārāyaṇa stands firm against a storm of rākṣasa arrows, resembling a mountain pelted by rain. He sounds the Pāñcajanya conch, scattering horses and chariots with its roar. When Māli strikes Garuḍa with a mace, the deity hurls his flaming cakra, severing the demon's head. The broken army flees toward Laṅkā, pursued by the wind of Garuḍa’s wings and volleys from the Śārṅga bow. Severed bodies and jewelry fall into the ocean, filling the sky like dark clouds.
chapters.subtitle: Viṣṇu defeats the rākṣasa army and kills Māli.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे अष्टमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Mālyavān turns to confront Nārāyaṇa, accusing him of attacking retreating foes. The god replies that he must destroy them to protect the deities. Mālyavān hurls a bell-clad śakti at the god’s chest; Nārāyaṇa returns the blow. After the rākṣasa strikes with a thorned iron javelin, Garuḍa flaps his wings, scattering the army like withered leaves. Beaten and ashamed, the rākṣasa leaders abandon Laṅkā and flee to pātāla, seeking refuge in the netherworld with their families.
chapters.subtitle: The rākṣasas flee to the underworld after defeat.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे नवमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sumālī instructs his daughter Kaikasī to wed the sage Viśravas. She approaches the ascetic during his agnihotra ritual at an inauspicious hour. She bears the ten-necked Daśagrīva, the large Kumbhakarṇa, the misshapen Śūrpaṇakhā, and the virtuous Vibhīṣaṇa. After seeing the golden carriage and wealth of her stepson Vaiśravaṇa, Kaikasī urges Daśagrīva to obtain similar power. Daśagrīva vows to surpass his brother and travels to the hermitage at Gokarṇa with his siblings to begin a period of austerity.
chapters.subtitle: Kaikasī marries Viśravas and gives birth to Rāvaṇa.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे दशमः सर्गः
chapters.es: The brothers undergo severe penances for ten thousand years. Kumbhakarṇa sits amidst fires and icy waters, while Vibhīṣaṇa stands on one leg to study the Veda. Daśagrīva sacrifices nine of his heads into the ritual flame. Appearing before them, Brahmā grants Daśagrīva protection from celestial beings and serpents. Vibhīṣaṇa chooses a mind fixed on dharma and receives immortality. Influenced by the goddess Sarasvatī, Kumbhakarṇa asks for long years of sleep. The brothers finally settle in the Śleṣmātaka woods.
chapters.subtitle: Three brothers receive boons from Brahmā.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकादशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sumālī and the rākṣasa leaders emerge from rasātala to meet Daśagrīva. They urge him to reclaim Laṅkā, their ancestral home now held by Vaiśravaṇa. Prahasta supports this, arguing that power overrides fraternal bonds. Following an embassy, Vaiśravaṇa consults his father, Viśravā, who describes Daśagrīva as cursed and commands his son to move to Kailāsa. Honoring his father, Vaiśravaṇa departs with his wealth and family. Daśagrīva then enters the empty city with his brothers and is installed as the new ruler.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa takes the city of Laṅkā from his brother.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे द्वादशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa gives his sister Śūrpaṇakhā in marriage to the demon Vidyujjihva. While wandering the forest, he meets Maya, who offers his daughter Mandodarī to the rākṣasa king. Maya also presents him with a śakti weapon, the spear later used against Lakṣmaṇa. After the fire-lit ceremony, Rāvaṇa returns to Laṅkā and secures wives for his brothers Kumbhakarṇa and Vibhīṣaṇa. Soon, Mandodarī gives birth to a son. Because the infant’s first cry rumbles like a storm cloud, shaking the city, his father names him Meghanāda.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa marries Mandodarī and Meghanāda is born.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे त्रयोदशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Kumbhakarṇa withdraws into a spacious mansion to sleep for thousands of years. In his absence, Rāvaṇa devastates the gardens of the gods and attacks the sages. A messenger arrives from Vaiśravaṇa, advising the king to abandon his violent path and recounting his friendship with Maheśvara. Enraged by this counsel, Rāvaṇa executes the envoy with a sword and offers the body to the rākṣasas. He then boards his chariot, intending to defeat his brother and seize control of the three worlds.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa kills an envoy and attacks his brother.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्दशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa reaches Mount Kailāsa with his six ministers to confront the forces of his brother. The Yakṣa army mobilizes like a surging ocean, meeting the rākṣasa advance with clubs and swords. Holding a mace resembling the kāladaṇḍa, Rāvaṇa cuts through the ranks, scattering defenders like wind-blown clouds. After the Yakṣa Saṃyodhakaṇṭaka strikes Mārīca with a discus, the rākṣasa recovers to drive him back. Rāvaṇa uproots a golden toraṇa to crush the gatekeeper Sūryabhānu, forcing the remaining Yakṣas to flee.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa defeats the Yakṣa army on Mount Kailāsa.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चदशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa leads his army against the Yakṣas on Mount Kailāsa. The general Māṇibhadra strikes the rākṣasa Dhūmrākṣa, but Rāvaṇa retaliates with a blow that tilts the Yakṣa’s crown. Kubera eventually enters the fray, rebuking his brother for his conduct and the fruits of karma. They exchange celestial weapons, including the āgneyāstra and vāruṇāstra. Finally, Rāvaṇa uses deceptive māyā to strike Kubera down with a mace. The victorious Rāvaṇa seizes the puṣpaka vimāna and departs the mountain in triumph.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa defeats Kubera and seizes the Puṣpaka vimāna.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे षोडशः सर्गः
chapters.es: The king of the rākṣasas encounters a mountain where his puṣpaka vimāna ceases to move. There, Nandiśvara warns him that Śaṅkara is at play. The king mocks Nandiśvara for his monkey-like face, prompting a curse that monkeys will eventually destroy the rākṣasa lineage. When the king attempts to uproot the mountain, Śaṅkara pins his arms beneath the rock with a big toe. His piercing cry earns him the name Rāvaṇa, and Śaṅkara eventually allows him to continue his journey.
chapters.subtitle: Śiva names Rāvaṇa after pinning him under a mountain.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे सप्तदशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa wanders the slopes of Himavān and encounters Vedavatī, a young woman wearing a deer-skin and matted locks. She explains her devotion to Viṣṇu and her life of asceticism. Overcome by lust, Rāvaṇa mocks her and seizes her hair. Angered, Vedavatī cuts her hair and prepares a funeral pyre. She vows to return in a future birth to cause his death. She enters the flames, eventually returning to earth as Sītā, born from a furrow in Janaka’s field.
chapters.subtitle: Vedavatī curses Rāvaṇa and vows to cause his death.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे अष्टादशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa ranges the earth on the puṣpaka vimāna and interrupts King Marutta’s sacrifice. Fearing the demon, the gods take animal forms: Indra becomes a peacock, Dharmarāja a crow, Varuṇa a swan, and Vaiśravaṇa a lizard. Although Marutta prepares for battle, the sage Saṃvarta forbids the fight to preserve the ritual. After Rāvaṇa departs, the gods reward these animals with permanent traits, such as the peacock’s many-eyed tail and the swan’s white feathers.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa interrupts a sacrifice and gods take animal forms.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकोनविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa travels the earth demanding submission from monarchs like Duṣyanta and Purūravas. In Ayodhyā, King Anaraṇya refuses to surrender and leads his elephants and horses into battle. When his army falls, Anaraṇya discharges eight hundred arrows at the rākṣasa’s head, but the shafts leave no wounds. Rāvaṇa strikes the king with his palm, casting him from his chariot. Before ascending to heaven, the dying Anaraṇya curses Rāvaṇa, prophesying that his descendant Rāma will eventually take the demon's life.
chapters.subtitle: King Anaraṇya curses Rāvaṇa before dying in battle.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे विंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Nārada descends upon a cloud to meet Rāvaṇa, who travels the earth in his puṣpaka vimāna. The sage observes that mortals already suffer from grief and attachment, making their slaughter unnecessary. Seeking a greater challenge, Rāvaṇa vows to conquer the lokapālas and destroy Yama, the god of death. He leads his ministers along the southern path toward the city of the dead. Nārada reflects on the power of time and follows the rākṣasa king to witness the coming battle.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa travels south to challenge the god of death.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Nārada travels to the abode of Yama, where the god of death judges the souls of the dead. Rāvaṇa arrives in his puṣpaka vimāna, illuminating the darkness. Seeing creatures suffering for their past deeds, the rākṣasa king forcibly liberates them. Enraged guards swarm the chariot with spears and maces. Though bloodied and forced to the ground, Rāvaṇa remains defiant. He looses the Pāśupata weapon, unleashing a flame that incinerates Yama’s army like a forest fire, leaving the battlefield trembling.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa invades the realm of Yama and releases the dead.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे द्वाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Vaivasvata mounts his chariot preceded by mṛtyu and the flaming kāladaṇḍa. While his ministers flee, Rāvaṇa stands firm, meeting spears with a rain of arrows. After seven nights of combat, Yama lifts his lethal staff to end the struggle. Brahmā intervenes, forbidding the strike to preserve the integrity of a previous boon. To avoid making the creator’s words false, Yama withdraws from the field and vanishes. The victorious rākṣasa king proclaims his name and departs in the puṣpaka vimāna.
chapters.subtitle: Brahmā stops the battle between Rāvaṇa and Yama.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa enters rasātala and subjugates the serpents of Bhogavatī. After combat with the Nivātakavaca Daityas, Brahmā brokers a peace, and the parties form an alliance where Rāvaṇa learns illusions. He then invades Varuṇa’s realm, passing the cow Surabhi to reach the water god’s palace. Varuṇa’s sons counterattack from the sky, but Mahodara destroys their chariots. Rāvaṇa overwhelms the princes with weapons. Learning Varuṇa is away in the realm of Brahmā, Rāvaṇa proclaims victory and returns to Laṅkā.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa makes alliances and defeats Varuṇa's sons.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa abducts the daughters of gods and sages, carrying them toward Laṅkā in the puṣpaka vimāna. These women weep for their slain families and curse him to meet his end through a woman. Upon entering the city, his sister Śūrpaṇakhā confronts him, lamenting the death of her husband at his hands. To appease her, Rāvaṇa sends her to the Daṇḍaka forest. He appoints Khara and an army to govern the region and protect her.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa abducts women and sends Śūrpaṇakhā to the forest.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa enters the Nikumbhilā grove to find his son, Meghanāda, completing seven Vedic sacrifices. The priest Uśanas lists the celestial chariot, tāmasī māyā, and inexhaustible quivers the youth received from Paśupati. Learning that the demon Madhu abducted his sister, Kumbhīnasī, Rāvaṇa leads an army to Madhupura. He spares Madhu after his sister begs for mercy. The two leaders then unite their forces, marching toward Mount Kailāsa to launch an assault against the celestial regions.
chapters.subtitle: Meghanāda performs sacrifices and Rāvaṇa spares Madhu.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे षड्विंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa camps his army amidst the fragrance of kadamba blossoms. He intercepts the apsarā Rambhā as she travels to meet her lover. Although she identifies as his snuṣā, the king ravishes her. Rambhā informs Nalakūbara of the assault, prompting him to curse Rāvaṇa: if he ever violates another unwilling woman, his head shall shatter into seven pieces. The gods rejoice at this news, and the king thereafter avoids forcing himself upon women.
chapters.subtitle: Nalakūbara curses Rāvaṇa after he assaults Rambhā.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे सप्तविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa leads his army past Mount Kailāsa to invade the celestial realm. Indra seeks counsel from Viṣṇu, who promises to cause the demon's death in the future despite his invincibility. During the battle, Sumālī routs the gods until the Vasu Sāvitra destroys his serpent-drawn chariot. Sāvitra then strikes Sumālī with a flaming mace, turning the rākṣasa to ash. Following this defeat, the rākṣasa army flees in panic, leaving the battlefield to the gods.
chapters.subtitle: The rākṣasa army invades heaven and Sumālī is killed.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे अष्टाविंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Meghanāda charges the divine army in a flaming chariot, scattering the gods with illusory darkness. Jayanta engages him until his grandfather, Pulomā, carries him to the safety of the ocean. Following his son’s disappearance, Indra enters the field on a chariot driven by Mātali, accompanied by the maruts and vasus. Rāvaṇa counters on a vehicle crafted by Viśvakarman. As Kumbhakarṇa strikes at the deities, a river of blood flows across the earth. Indra and Rāvaṇa exchange arrow volleys.
chapters.subtitle: The gods and rākṣasas fight each other in battle.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकोनत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Darkness descends as rākṣasas and celestials clash. Rāvaṇa drives his chariot through the divine ranks to slay the gods. Recognizing Rāvaṇa’s invulnerability due to a boon, Indra attempts to capture him alive. Amidst the chaos, Meghanāda uses māyā to vanish from sight. He strikes the charioteer Mātali, forcing Indra to mount the elephant Airāvata. Meghanāda binds Indra with illusory fetters and carries the captive to his city, while Rāvaṇa follows to celebrate his son's victory.
chapters.subtitle: Meghanāda captures Indra in battle using illusory powers.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Brahmā travels to Laṅkā to negotiate the release of Indra, whom Rāvaṇa’s son has captured. He names the prince Indrajit and grants a boon ensuring his victory if he finishes a fire sacrifice before fighting. Once freed, a dejected Indra learns that his defeat resulted from Gautama’s curse following the violation of Ahalyā. Following Brahmā’s counsel, Indra performs a vaiṣṇava sacrifice to cleanse himself of this sin. He then returns to his throne and resumes his reign.
chapters.subtitle: Brahmā names Indrajit and Indra performs a sacrifice.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa arrives at Māhiṣmatī to challenge the Haihaya king, Arjuna, but finds him away at the Narmadā river. After traversing the Vindhya peaks, the rākṣasa leader reaches the riverbank. While his ministers gather blossoms, Rāvaṇa bathes and recites prayers. He establishes a golden liṅga on a sandy altar, offering flowers and incense. The ritual concludes as he dances with uplifted hands and sings in praise of Śiva.
chapters.subtitle: Rāvaṇa visits the Narmadā river and worships Śiva.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे द्वात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa offers flowers on the banks of the Narmadā while Kārtavīryārjuna sports with his wives nearby. The king blocks the river’s flow with his thousand arms, causing the water to surge backward and sweep away the demon’s offerings. Enraged, Rāvaṇa initiates a battle. After Arjuna strikes down Prahasta with a club, he engages Rāvaṇa in a duel of maces. Arjuna overwhelms his opponent, binds the ten-headed king, and leads the captive into Māhiṣmatī.
chapters.subtitle: Arjuna captures Rāvaṇa after blocking the Narmadā river.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे त्रयस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Pulastya travels through the air to Māhiṣmatī after hearing of Rāvaṇa’s capture. King Arjuna receives the sage with madhuparka and water, bowing low. When Pulastya requests his grandson’s freedom, Arjuna releases the rākṣasa and honors him with ornaments and robes. They establish friendship before an agni. Rāvaṇa departs while Pulastya returns to the heavens. Though once bound, the freed rākṣasa king soon resumes his conquest and continues to distress the inhabitants of the earth.
chapters.subtitle: Pulastya secures the release of Rāvaṇa from Arjuna.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāvaṇa arrives at Kiṣkindhā seeking battle but finds Vālī at the southern ocean performing sandhyā rites. As Rāvaṇa attempts a stealthy capture, Vālī seizes him and pinions the rākṣasa king under his arm. Vālī leaps through the sky, visiting the four great oceans to finish his prayers while his captive remains helpless. Upon returning to Kiṣkindhā, Vālī releases his prisoner. Struck by this display of power, Rāvaṇa requests an alliance, and the two monarchs swear friendship before a ritual fire.
chapters.subtitle: Vālī captures Rāvaṇa and the two become allies.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Agastya recounts Hanumān’s past strength to Rāma. Agastya describes the monkey’s childhood leap toward the sun, mistaken for a fruit. After chasing Rāhu and charging at the elephant Airāvata, Hanumān falls when Indra strikes him with a vajra. The blow breaks the child’s jaw, the hanu. In retaliation, Vāyu withdraws the breath of all living creatures, paralyzing the worlds. Gods and mortals follow Brahmā to appease the grieving wind deity as he cradles his injured son.
chapters.subtitle: Indra strikes Hanumān and Vāyu stops all breath.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Brahmā revives the infant Hanumān with a touch, prompting Vāyu to restore the vital breath of all creatures. To appease the wind god, the deities bestow boons that render the child invulnerable to divine weapons and grant him mastery over the śāstra. Growing unruly, Hanumān disturbs the forest hermitages until sages curse him to forget his own strength. He eventually becomes the inseparable companion of Sugrīva, living in ignorance of his power until the time comes to oppose Rāvaṇa.
chapters.subtitle: Hanumān receives divine boons and a sage's curse.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे सप्तत्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma embraces Pratardana, the king of Kāśī, and instructs him to return to Vārāṇasī. Turning to the three hundred assembled kings, Rāma attributes the destruction of Rāvaṇa to their collective power, describing himself as a mere instrument in the battle. He acknowledges their loyalty during the search for Sītā and grants them leave to return home. The kings celebrate his victory and stable reign before bidding him a respectful farewell.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma dismisses the allied kings after his coronation.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे अष्टात्रिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Allied kings depart for their kingdoms, sending gifts of horses, elephants, and sandalwood to Ayodhyā. Rāma accepts these treasures only to distribute them among Sugrīva, Vibhīṣaṇa, and the vānara chiefs. The guests decorate themselves with jewels and feast on honey and meat. They remain in the city throughout the śaiśira season, where two months pass as they enjoy the company of Rāghava.
chapters.subtitle: The kings depart and Rāma rewards his allies.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकोनचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma instructs Sugrīva to return to Kiṣkindhā and govern alongside his ministers. He then directs Vibhīṣaṇa to rule Laṅkā with righteousness, reminding him to avoid unpious thoughts. Hanumān vows to remain on earth as long as the rāmakathā is told. In response, Rāma embraces him and fastens a chain of vaidūrya stones around his neck. The assembled monkeys and rākṣasas touch Rāma’s feet and depart for their homes, weeping as they leave their leader.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma sends his allies home and embraces Hanumān.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma resides with his brothers after his allies depart. The puṣpaka vimāna descends from the sky, explaining that Kubera has returned it to serve Rāma following the defeat of Rāvaṇa. Rāma honors the vehicle with flowers and incense, instructing it to return whenever summoned. Bharata reports the prosperity of the realm, noting that children are born healthy and rains fall in their proper season. The citizens celebrate this period of health and abundance.
chapters.subtitle: The puṣpaka vimāna returns and the kingdom prospers.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma enters the Aśokavanikā and sits with Sītā, offering her madhu-maireya wine as attendants serve meat and fruit. Following his royal duties, he observes signs of pregnancy in Sītā and offers to fulfill any desire. She requests to visit the tapovana along the Gaṅgā to spend a night among the sages. Rāma grants her wish, promising her departure for the following morning before he joins his companions.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma promises Sītā a visit to the forest sages.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे द्विचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma sits with his councillors and listening to various tales. He asks his companion Bhadra to report the honest opinions of the citizens regarding his family and reign. Bhadra describes how the people praise the ocean bridge but question Rāma for welcoming Sītā home after her stay in the Aśokavanikā. The subjects fear they must now tolerate similar conduct from their own wives. Distressed, Rāma confirms the rumors with his friends and dismisses them.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma hears the public's criticism regarding Sītā.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे त्रिचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma dismisses his companions and sends a messenger to summon Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, and Śatrughna. The brothers arrive in white robes to find Rāma with a downcast face and eyes wet with tears like a moon eclipsed by Rāhu. They touch his feet in greeting. After wiping his eyes, Rāma embraces them and leads them to their seats. He explains that they are his very life and asks them to help him fulfill his royal duties.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma summons his brothers to discuss the slander.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma addresses his brothers, recounting the public slander regarding Sītā. Though he affirms her purity witnessed by the gods at Laṅkā, he prioritizes his family's reputation. He commands Lakṣmaṇa to take Sītā by chariot to the banks of the Gaṅgā. He orders that she be left near the hermitage of Vālmīki under the pretense of fulfilling her wish to visit the forest, then retreats to his quarters in tears.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma orders Lakṣmaṇa to abandon Sītā in the forest.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa instructs Sumantra to prepare a horse-drawn chariot for a journey to the forest. Believing she is visiting sages, Sītā gathers costly robes and jewels as gifts. As they travel, she notices her right eye trembling and prays to the deities for the welfare of the royal family. They rest near the Gomatī river before reaching the banks of the Bhāgīrathī. Distressed, Lakṣmaṇa weeps, while Sītā encourages him to prepare a boat for their crossing.
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa leads Sītā toward the hermitage of Vālmīki.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे षट्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa leads Sītā into a fisherman’s boat and crosses the Bhāgīrathī. On the far bank, he falls to the ground with folded palms and a voice choked by tears. He reveals that the king, fearing public censure, has ordered her abandonment despite her innocence. Lakṣmaṇa leaves her near the tapovana of the sage Vālmīki on the banks of the Jāhnavī. He instructs her to seek shelter with the forest-dwelling sage.
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa leaves Sītā on the banks of the Jāhnavī.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे सप्तचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sītā collapses on the riverbank upon hearing Lakṣmaṇa announce her exile. She laments her fate but refuses to drown in the Jāhnavī to protect the royal lineage. She sends a final message to Rāma, urging him to rule his subjects like brothers. Lakṣmaṇa bows in silence, recrosses the river, and watches from his chariot. Left alone, Sītā cries out in the forest as the peacocks call around her, abandoned despite her purity.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā reacts to her exile and sends a message.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे अष्टचत्वारिंशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Young ascetics find a woman wailing by the Jāhnavī and alert Vālmīki. The sage approaches Sītā with an arghya and reveals that his spiritual vision has already confirmed her innocence and identity. He leads the daughter of Janaka to his forest home, presenting her to the resident female ascetics. Vālmīki commands them to protect her with maternal care. Sītā accepts this sanctuary, and the sage returns to his retreat while the women welcome her.
chapters.subtitle: Vālmīki discovered Sītā and offers her refuge.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकोनपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa expresses his grief to the charioteer Sumantra after leaving Sītā at the hermitage. He questions the injustice of the exile and attributes Rāma’s suffering to the power of daiva. Sumantra consoles him by revealing a secret prophecy spoken by the sage Durvāsas to King Daśaratha. He explains that Rāma is destined to endure separation and will eventually renounce his brothers and his wife. Lakṣmaṇa urges the charioteer to recount the full details.
chapters.subtitle: Sumantra consoles Lakṣmaṇa with a secret prophecy.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sumantra recounts to Lakṣmaṇa a meeting between King Daśaratha and the sage Durvāsā at Vasiṣṭha’s hermitage. Daśaratha questioned the sage about the fate of his lineage. Durvāsā foretold that Rāma would rule for eleven thousand years but would endure a separation from Sītā. He predicted Rāma’s performance of multiple aśvamedha sacrifices and his final departure to the realm of Brahmā. Sumantra shares this prophecy to steady Lakṣmaṇa as they rest on the banks of the Gomatī.
chapters.subtitle: Sumantra recounts Durvāsā’s prophecy regarding Rāma.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Lakṣmaṇa leaves the Gomatī at dawn and enters Ayodhyā by midday. He finds Rāma weeping in his palace. Touching his brother's feet, Lakṣmaṇa reports that Sītā now stays at the āśrama of Vālmīki. To ease the king's sorrow, he cites the truth that all saṃyoga ends in separation and life ends in death. He urges Rāma to use his own mind to overcome this grief. Rāma finds comfort in these words and thanks his brother.
chapters.subtitle: Lakṣmaṇa returns to Ayodhyā and consoles Rāma.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे द्विपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sumantra announces the arrival of over one hundred sages from the banks of the Yamunā, led by Cyavana. Rāma welcomes the ascetics into the palace, accepting their gifts of water and fruit. He seats them on golden grass mats and pledges his life and kingdom to fulfill their needs. The sages praise Rāma for committing his help before even hearing their request. They ask for protection from a specific danger, noting that Rāma honors his duty to the brāhmaṇas.
chapters.subtitle: Sages from the Yamunā ask Rāma for protection.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे त्रिपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Sages approach Rāma to request protection from the rākṣasa Lavaṇa. Bhārgava recounts how Rudra once granted a flaming śūla to the asura Madhu for his piety. This weapon reduces enemies to ashes before returning to its owner. Madhu passed the spear to his son, Lavaṇa, who now uses its power to slaughter ascetics and terrorize the worlds. Having heard of Rāvaṇa’s defeat, the sages seek Rāma's help to end this threat.
chapters.subtitle: The sages describe the rākṣasa Lavaṇa and his trident.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे चतुःपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma questions the sages about Lavaṇa, a rākṣasa who haunts Madhuvana and devours forest animals and ascetics. When Rāma seeks a volunteer to slay the demon, Bharata offers his services. Śatrughna intercedes, arguing that Bharata already endured years of hardship in Nandigrāma. Rāma grants Śatrughna the mission and declares him the future king of the demon’s territory. He then initiates a formal abhiṣeka, calling upon Vasiṣṭha to perform the consecration rites.
chapters.subtitle: Śatrughna is chosen to slay Lavaṇa and rule.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Śatrughna accepts his brother’s command with humility. Rāma directs Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa to assemble priests and ministers for Śatrughna’s abhiṣeka. After the ritual, Rāma seats Śatrughna on his lap and presents a divine arrow once used against the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha. He warns that Lavaṇa wields a śūla gifted by Śiva, which renders him invincible while held. Śatrughna must intercept the rākṣasa at the city gates while he is weaponless.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma gives Śatrughna a divine arrow to kill Lavaṇa.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma provides Śatrughna with thousands of horses, chariots, and elephants. The army must cross the Jāhnavī river before summer ends and wait for the rainy season to strike Lavaṇa. Śatrughna instructs his commanders to avoid oppressing the people during their march. After bowing to Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and Kaikeyī, he circumambulates his brothers and the priest Vasiṣṭha before departing for Madhuvana with his bow.
chapters.subtitle: Śatrughna departs for Madhuvana with a large army.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Śatrughna arrives at the hermitage of Vālmīki and receives a welcome of fruits and roots. Noticing a nearby sacrificial ground, he asks about its history. Vālmīki recounts how their ancestor King Saudāsa killed a tiger-shaped rākṣasa, whose companion later sought revenge. Disguised as the sage Vasiṣṭha, the demon tricked the king into serving human meat, leading to a twelve-year curse. After the king fulfilled this sentence, he returned to his throne.
chapters.subtitle: Vālmīki tells Śatrughna the story of King Saudāsa.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे अष्टपञ्चाशः सर्गः
chapters.es: Śatrughna stays in a thatched cottage the night Sītā gives birth to twin sons. At midnight, Vālmīki performs a protective rakṣā rite using kuśa grass and its lower lava segments to purify the infants, naming them Kuśa and Lava. Hearing the news and the chanting of Rāma’s name, Śatrughna rejoices through the night. He departs the next morning, traveling to reach a hermitage on the banks of the Yamunā, where he joins the resident sages.
chapters.subtitle: Sītā gives birth to twin sons in the hermitage.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकोनषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Śatrughna asks the sage Cyavana about the power of Lavaṇa and his śūla. Cyavana recounts how King Māndhātā once sought Indra’s throne. Indra challenged him to first subdue Lavaṇa, who remained independent in Madhuvana. When Māndhātā attacked, the rākṣasa devoured the royal messenger and released his flaming śūla. The weapon reduced the king and his army to ashes. Cyavana advises Śatrughna to strike tomorrow morning, catching the rākṣasa while he is unarmed.
chapters.subtitle: Cyavana explains the power of Lavaṇa’s trident.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे षष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Śatrughna crosses the Yamunā and waits at the gates of Madhupura with his bow. At midday, the rākṣasa Lavaṇa returns carrying the carcasses of many creatures. Seeing the armed prince, Lavaṇa laughs and mocks the death of Rāvaṇa, claiming he previously spared the brothers out of contempt. Śatrughna radiates heat from his limbs in anger and identifies himself as the son of Daśaratha. He rejects the rākṣasa's request to fetch a weapon, refusing to let a foe escape.
chapters.subtitle: Śatrughna challenges the unarmed Lavaṇa at the city gate.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Lavaṇa hurls trees at Śatrughna, striking him unconscious. The rākṣasa neglects his śūla to gather food, believing his foe dead. Śatrughna recovers and draws a divine arrow once used by Viṣṇu against Madhu and Kaiṭabha. As its light terrifies the gods, Śatrughna fires the shaft through Lavaṇa’s chest into rasātala. The rākṣasa falls like a mountain struck by lightning. With Lavaṇa slain, the śūla returns to Rudra, and Śatrughna shines like the sun.
chapters.subtitle: Śatrughna kills Lavaṇa with a divine arrow.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे द्विषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: After the death of Lavaṇa, the gods grant Śatrughna a boon. He requests that Madhupurī become his capital, and the gods name the region Śūrasena. Śatrughna summons his army from the Gaṅgā to begin construction during the month of Śrāvaṇa. Within twelve years, a city shaped like a half-moon or ardhacandra rises along the Yamunā. The new capital, Madhurā, fills with houses and trade. With the kingdom secure, Śatrughna decides to travel and visit Rāma.
chapters.subtitle: Śatrughna builds the city of Madhurā.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे त्रिषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: After twelve years, Śatrughna returns to Ayodhyā to visit Rāma. He reports his victory over Lavaṇa and the successful settlement of his city. Expressing the pain of separation, he asks to stay, but Rāma reminds him that kṣatriyadharma demands a king remain with his subjects. Śatrughna stays for five nights before departing in a horse-drawn chariot. Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa walk alongside him for a distance as he begins his journey back to his own realm.
chapters.subtitle: Śatrughna visits Rāma before returning to his kingdom.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे चतुःषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: An old brāhmaṇa arrives at the palace gate carrying the body of his young son. He weeps and laments that the child met an untimely death despite the father’s own sinless conduct. The grieving man directly blames Rāma for the tragedy, asserting that a king’s hidden faults lead to such unnatural calamities. He demands that the king restore the boy to life, claiming that under a righteous ruler, no child should die before his parents.
chapters.subtitle: A brāhmaṇa blames Rāma for his son’s death.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma summons Vasiṣṭha and several sages to address a brāhmaṇa’s grief. Nārada explains that the world has declined from the Kṛta Yuga, an age where only brāhmaṇas performed tapas. He reveals that a Śūdra is currently practicing forbidden asceticism in the kingdom, an act of adharma that has caused the child’s untimely death. To restore life to the boy, Nārada advises Rāma to find the individual responsible for this violation and suppress the unlawful penance.
chapters.subtitle: Nārada identifies a Śūdra’s penance as the cause.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे षट्षष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma instructs Lakṣmaṇa to preserve the deceased child's body in a tailadroṇī filled with fragrant oils. Summoning the puṣpaka vimāna, Rāma arms himself and travels across the four quarters to locate the source of the kingdom's transgression. He finds no fault in the west, north, or east. Reaching the south near the Śaivala mountain, he discovers an ascetic performing penance while hanging upside down. Rāma approaches the practitioner to question his identity.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma searches for the source of the kingdom's adharma.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे सप्तषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: Rāma confronts the Śūdra ascetic Śambūka, who seeks to reach heaven through penance. Rāma draws his sword and beheads him, immediately restoring life to a dead brāhmaṇa child. Following this, Rāma visits the forest hermitage of the sage Agastya. The sage welcomes him with hospitality and gifts him a radiant ornament forged by Viśvakarman. Rāma accepts the celestial jewelry and asks the sage to explain its origin, prompting Agastya to begin a narrative.
chapters.subtitle: Rāma executes Śambūka and visits Agastya.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे अष्टषष्टितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: During the tretāyuga, an ascetic enters a silent forest and finds a fresh corpse in a lake. A figure arrives in a swan-drawn vimāna attended by apsarases. The visitor descends, devours the flesh of the body, and bathes in the water. Before the traveler can depart, the witness questions why a being of such heavenly appearance consumes a foul meal. The ascetic demands to know the traveler’s identity and the reason for this unsettling act.
chapters.subtitle: Agastya recounts seeing a heavenly being eat a corpse.

chapters.name: उत्तरकाण्डे एकोनसप्ततितमः सर्गः
chapters.es: King Śveta explains why he must consume his own corpse despite residing in Brahmaloka. Although he ruled piously and performed long penance, he neglected the practice of dāna, leaving his soul famished. Following the counsel of Brahmā, he returns to a forest lake daily to feed on his former body.
